title: International Internship: Early Childhood (Birth-12 Years)
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: In this course, teacher education students will prepare a professional portfolio based on their internship that demonstrates their applied knowledge and skills of teaching and learning and pedagogical leadership. They will refine their personal philosophy as an early childhood and primary school educator; explore the legal, social and ethical responsibilities associated with being a member of the teaching profession across both sectors; and consider their responsibility as educators in their home country communities through the application of Action learning/Action research. The course requires students to undertake 10 days observation (5 days in an Early Childhood setting and 5 days in a Primary School) and 40 days of supervised practice in an Early Childhood setting (the definition of which may vary according to the jurisdictional requirements). The teacher education student will be responsible for up to two-thirds of their mentor educator's teaching load during this placement. Teacher education students will interact and contribute to the setting and its community.
learning_outcomes: Construct, implement and evaluate unit/s of work that are responsive to the needs of the school and community.
Engage in critical reflection on their development and learning as an ethical teacher in productive professional learning communities.

Develop strategies for identifying professional learning strengths and needs, critical reflection, individual and collegial support, engagement with the wider school community and the world beyond the classroom/school.
Engage in the full life of the educational setting they are placed in.
Demonstrate progress towards the attainment of Graduate Teacher Standards through professional experience.

title: Extended Studies in Health and Physical Education
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course builds on the premise that beginning teachers need to be reflective practitioners and inquirers. Through engagement with the new national Health and Physical Education curriculum, this course builds on curriculum concepts, theories, issues and practices introduced in previous teaching and learning courses, to further develop students theoretical and practical skills in program and assessment development in HPE. Furthermore, the course intends to provide students with the opportunities to understand group processes in curriculum development and management skills in enacting such development. As a result of engagement in seminar style presentations and problem-based assessment tasks, students should develop contemporary understandings of curriculum and assessment issues in HPE, as well as be introduced to professional issues and organisations pertinent to their work as a beginning HPE teacher.
learning_outcomes: Research contemporary resources that evaluate the effectiveness and purpose of HPE professional development for career trajectory.

Clarify the educational value orientations that underpin teaching and learning in HPE secondary school settings and be equipped with the knowledge and skills to defend and/or justify those educational values.
Refine skills in evaluating and synthesizing information/knowledge from curriculum documents and other relevant literature in terms of quality programming, assessment and teaching practice
Work as both independent and collaborative, self-motivated problem solvers
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of a wide range of contemporary issues relevant to teaching HPE.

title: Senior Technology 4 Curriculum Methods
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course provides an introduction to curriculum, pedagogy and assessment and NESA requirements for teaching Stage 6 Technology Syllabi. It provides students with an opportunity to understand the various discourses on current issues that inform teachers' knowledge and pedagogical practice, as well as critically engaging with models of pedagogy.
learning_outcomes: Understand issues involved in managing and supervising senior technology projects.
Utilise appropriate pedagogies, resources, and assessment practices for teaching Stage 6 Technology
Understand the assessment requirements of the NSW Higher School Certificate.
Design challenging, engaging, and supportive scope and sequence and units for teaching the Stage 6 Technology curriculum of their first and/or second teaching areas.

title: International Internship: Primary
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: In this course, teacher education students will prepare a professional portfolio based on their internship that demonstrates their applied knowledge and skills of teaching and learning and pedagogical leadership. They will refine their personal philosophy as a primary school educator; explore the legal, social and ethical responsibilities associated with being a member of the teaching profession; and consider their responsibility as a primary teacher in their home country communities through the application of Action learning/Action research. The course requires students to undertake 5 days observation and 50 days of supervised practice in a Primary school setting. The observation is included in the 50 days supervised practice. The teacher education student will be responsible for up to two-thirds of their mentor educator's teaching load during this placement. Teacher education students will interact and contribute to the School and its community.
learning_outcomes: Develop strategies for identifying professional learning strengths and needs, critical reflection, individual and collegial support, engagement with the wider school community and the world beyond the classroom/school.
Construct, implement and evaluate unit/s of work that are responsive to the needs of the school and community.
Demonstrate the attainment of all Graduate Teacher Standards through professional experience.

Design and implement authentic learning tasks integrating cross-curricular capabilities.
Engage in the full life of school including student sport, playground supervision, faculty/grade/stage meetings and school activities and functions.

title: Advanced Literacy Studies
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course will explore current research on children's language acquisition and the teaching, learning and assessment of reading (including phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, and text comprehension); instructional approaches for developing children's concepts of print, grammar, punctuation, spelling and handwriting; and strategies for teaching and assessing the composition of digital and multi-modal texts. Students will learn how to interpret school-based and system-wide literacy data, and to consider related issues of literacy practices in the home, child language development, the diverse language backgrounds of students, intercultural awareness, and inclusiveness, in order to make informed decisions about student literacy needs.
learning_outcomes: Describe the importance of home and community literacy and numeracy practices.

Apply a range of models of pedagogy for teaching and assessing the components of reading (including strategies for teaching and assessing phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, and text comprehension).
Explain the purpose of providing timely and appropriate feedback to students about their learning.
Analyse evidence based research and apply findings to support the interpretation of school-based and system-wide literacy data.
Apply instructional approaches for developing children's concepts of print, grammar, punctuation, spelling and handwriting

Apply the principles and practices of teaching English as an Additional Language or Dialect (EAL/D) and supporting students with learning difficulties to design and implement units of work for diverse K-6 contexts

title: International Internship: Secondary
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: In this course, teacher education students will prepare a professional portfolio based on their internship that demonstrates their applied knowledge and skills of teaching and learning. They will refine their personal philosophy as a secondary school educator; explore the legal, social and ethical responsibilities associated with being a member of the teaching profession; and consider their responsibility as secondary teacher in their home country communities through the application of Action learning/Action research. The course requires students to undertake 5 days observation and 50 days of supervised practice in a Secondary school setting. The observation is included in the 50 days supervised practice. The teacher education student will be responsible for up to two-thirds of their mentor educator's teaching load during this placement. Teacher education students will interact and contribute to the School and its community.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the attainment of all Graduate Teacher Standards through professional experience.

Develop strategies for identifying professional learning strengths and needs, critical reflection, individual and collegial support, engagement with the wider school community and the world beyond the classroom/school.
Construct, implement and evaluate unit/s of work that are responsive to the needs of the school and community.
Design and implement authentic learning tasks for their specialist subject area/s.
Engage in critical reflection on their development and learning as an ethical teacher in productive professional learning communities.
Engage in the full life of school including student sport, playground supervision, faculty/grade/stage meetings and school activities and functions.

title: K-6 Curriculum Contexts: Integration and Inclusion
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course addresses professional skill development in curriculum design through professional engagement and reflection on and for action.
learning_outcomes: Identify issues of context to direct curriculum design.
Plan strategies to engage community in curriculum implementation.
Identify assets of community to construct curriculum.
Communicate effectively with community to engage in planning and implementation of curriculum.

title: Education in Global Perspective: Issues for Australian teachers
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course is designed to prepare teachers to successfully work in diverse learning environments in Australia and abroad and to prepare for leadership roles in education policy and governance. It introduces pre-service teachers to global issues in education with a focus on initiatives for diversity, equity, and innovation. Students will acquire a socio-historical and comparative understanding about the global expansion of mass education and contemporary challenges related to transnational flows of people, ideas, and resources. They will increase their knowledge about diverse geographical and political world regions, and accompanying educational traditions. Through project-based tasks, students will acquire an in-depth knowledge about education in a country of their choice. In addition, they will develop the skills and capacity to use different kinds of educational data for comparative analyses of international education policy and practice.
learning_outcomes: Develop critical media literacy skills to construct informed comparisons between educational contexts in Australia and other countries.
Apply different kinds of educational data to research successful international and global initiatives for equity and diversity;
Work collaboratively on a project-based learning task.
Engage with and teach about cultural diversity and equity;
Understand diverse educational systems and practices in historical and cultural context;
Develop an in-depth case study on educational issue of their choice;

title: Media Arts Learning in Primary School: An Integrated Approach
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with the creative and critical knowledge and skills to become arts education leaders in schools and communities. This course introduces key concepts and approaches of trans-disciplinarity, focussing on how Creative Arts education acts as a powerful pedagogical force for worlding futures and strengthening learning communities, where the aim is to foster children’s imaginations and agency, deepening their understandings and experiences of creativity, care, justice, peace, and human rights. Transdisciplinary arts projects can enhance and celebrate the collective imagination by involving participants in creative and active learning that help to build their own capacities for futuring and relating to changing worlds and times. The course focusses on educators as important and creative thought leaders and change agents, as they create meaningful participatory arts projects in schools and communities. Through inquiry-based learning, collaboration and student-centred pedagogy, students will design, create and implement transdisciplinary arts projects and build their skills as creative teaching artists and arts educators.
learning_outcomes: Create and lead rich arts learning experiences that strengthen young peoples’ imaginations and creative agency as active players and meaning makers in their own worlds and futures.
Effectively use and apply a range of arts processes and practices for the benefit of students’ creative and critical learning development.
Use and apply the knowledge and skills of transdisciplinary Creative Arts praxis to create and lead innovative blended participatory arts learning processes and projects in schools and communities.
Engage in critical reflection and analysis of experiential arts education processes and projects.

title: Civics and Citizenship Education
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course is intended to enable students to develop and extend understandings of the links between education and citizenship. During the course students investigate the contrasting notions of citizenship operating through curriculum materials. Particular attention will be given to values of education and/or conceptions of active citizenship and how these can be implemented in primary schools.
learning_outcomes: Locate, critique and review values and/or citizenship educational resources and programs;
Demonstrate knowledge of the key principles and practices associated with Australian civic knowledge;
Articulate how to differentiate the curriculum to cater for varying levels of civics and active citizenship expertise in primary school.

Articulate the different conceptions of civics and citizenship education as manifested in terms like civics, citizenship education, active citizenship, global citizenship and to consider the practical application of these various conceptions;

title: Education Honours I: Introduction to Education Research
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course is an introduction to fundamental discussions and concepts in educational research. Students will engage with key debates in the philosophy of social science and consider the role of theory in educational research.
learning_outcomes: Understand competing traditions of education research and the implications for research design
Understand key issues in the philosophy of social science including recognising how different paradigms conceptualise knowledge, validity and the researchers' position
Understand the role of theory in research and become familiar with some of the major contemporary theoretical perspectives in educational research

title: Education Honours II: Research Design and Methods
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course provides an introduction to educational research with a view to developing an aligned perspective of research design, theory and methods. Students will engage with key questions of data collection, data analysis and ethical conduct in education research.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and produce research project designs
Understand analysis processes of various research data/ materials
Be knowledgeable of what constitutes ethical conduct in research involving humans
Understand key features of major research methods in education

title: Honours III - Thesis A
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course is the first of two courses that involve students in the design and conduct of an independent research project and the production of a written thesis. The project and thesis must sit within the field of educational scholarship and research.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse educational research and scholarship.
Demonstrate a capacity to conduct an independent research project.
Work effectively with a research mentor or supervisor.

title: Honours IV - Thesis B
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course is the second of two courses that involve students in the design and conduct of an independent research project and the production of a written thesis. The project and thesis must sit within the field of educational scholarship and research.
learning_outcomes: Work effectively with a research mentor or supervisor.
Demonstrate a capacity to conduct and complete an independent research project.
Write up research in the form of a thesis or report of no less than 12,000 words.
Critically analyse educational research and scholarship.

title: Honours III - Thesis A
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course is the first of two courses that involve students in the design and conduct of an independent research project and the production of a written thesis. The project and thesis must sit within the field of educational scholarship and research.
learning_outcomes: Work effectively with a research mentor or supervisor.
Demonstrate a capacity to conduct an independent research project.
Critically analyse educational research and scholarship.

title: Senior Social Sciences Curriculum Methods
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course explores current issues and trends in teaching and learning Society & Culture, Aboriginal Studies, Studies of Religion, Geography, Economics, Business Studies, and Legal Studies in NSW secondary schools. Students will explore the role and value of HSIE curriculum; the K-12 HSIE learning continuum; and their contribution to civics and citizenship education. Students will explore lesson planning, programming, course and assessment requirements of the NSW Higher School Certificate; and strategies, technologies, and resources for teaching and learning their speciality senior social science subjects. Particular attention will also be given to the overlapping concepts operating within these curricula.
learning_outcomes: Develop lesson plans, programs and assessment tasks for Stage 6 Senior Social Science subjects.
Discuss the role and value of studying the Senior Social Sciences; their place within the NSW K-12 HSIE learning continuum; and contribution to civics and citizenship education.
Use a range of strategies, technologies and resources for teaching and assessing Stage 6 Senior Social Science.
Understand the overlapping concepts operating within Society & Culture, Aboriginal Studies, Studies of Religion, Geography, Economics, Business Studies & Legal Studies curricula.
Discuss current issues and trends related to the teaching of the Senior Social Sciences in schools.

title: Honours IV - Thesis B
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course is the second of two courses that involve students in the design and conduct of an independent research project and the production of a written thesis. The project and thesis must sit within the field of educational scholarship and research.
learning_outcomes: Work effectively with a research mentor or supervisor.
Demonstrate a capacity to conduct and complete an independent research project.
Write up research in the form of a thesis or report of no less than 12,000 words.
Critically analyse educational research and scholarship.

title: Understanding Aspirations for Greater Equity
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course provides a comprehensive account of the concept of aspirations, emphasising the role of teachers and school leaders in shaping and nurturing students’ post-school aspirations. It explores current issues relating to access to higher education for traditionally under-represented groups, with a particular focus on Indigenous Australians, people from low socio-economic status backgrounds, women in non-traditional areas of study, people living in regional and remote areas of Australia, and first-in-family students. Participants will: engage with Australian and international research exploring the educational and occupational aspirations of school students; identify the various factors that influence aspirations including intersections among factors; and, develop a sound theoretical and empirical basis for translating the concept of aspirations into classroom and school practice.
learning_outcomes: Recognise and explain the different ways that teachers and schools explicitly and implicitly influence post-school aspirations.
Identify factors that play a role in aspiration formation.
Translate the concept of aspirations into specific plans for classroom and school practice.
Explain the concept of aspirations, taking into account the historical and contemporary policy context.
Analyse and discuss current issues relating to the under-representation of particular groups of students in Australian higher education.
Develop a conceptual framework for theorising the concept of aspirations

title: Social Justice and Early Childhood Education
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course will challenge participants' constructions of identity, difference, diversity, and social inequalities in relation to local and global experiences. Participants will critically engage with a range of theoretical approaches through a social justice lens, with a focus on poverty as it impacts upon children, families and community. Furthermore, the course will address recent theoretical developments in social constructions of race, gender, disability, and sexuality. Participants will apply theoretical knowledge to investigate, analyse and synthesise social justice issues in their chosen disciplines of early childhood education, family or community development studies. This will result in a complex body of knowledge that re-examines participants' philosophies and articulates socially transformative practices for children, their families and communities.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine socially transformative practices in a nominated context that addresses the needs of children, families, and their communities.
Articulate social justice theories in terms of children, families and community, specifically the impact of poverty.
Investigate a nominated context in early childhood education, family and/or community to analyse and synthesise the theory/practice nexus.
Recognise ethical practices as a basis for social justice.
Critique current theorizing on the social constructions of race, gender, disability, and sexuality.
Challenge contemporary ideas about identity, difference and diversity.

title: Contemporary Issues and Early Childhood
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: It is widely recognised in early years research that the first years of a child's life are vitally important to their overall growth and development. These early years have life long effects for children's well being. For children, families and early years educators, these years are impacted through a range of complex issues such as family context, health, poverty, disability, gender, culture, environmental sustainability, policy developments and the range of rituals and customs associated with child rearing. This course critically investigates and analyses these issues within a framework of children's rights and participation.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate critical engagement with the theories, philosophies and approaches to early years provision.
Develop, articulate and justify a professional/leadership position regarding early childhood and early years provision; and
Demonstrate a critical awareness and understanding of various contemporary issues in early childhood, including children's rights and participation;

title: Advanced Educational Studies 1
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course is offered to students who are interested in developing a specialised education research topic under the supervision of the course coordinator. Students will work on their chosen topic to conduct thorough literature research as an important step in educational research to explore the trends and current development of the research literature as well as to establish their levels of advanced understanding of the topic.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding and knowledge of their specific topic.
Critically review the current published research literature on their specific topic.
Identify areas of prior scholarship and gaps in their specific topic.

title: Advanced Curriculum Methods
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course equips students with advanced curriculum methods for teaching in an additional subject area. It focuses on course design, programming, and assessment aligned with relevant educational frameworks, such as the National Assessment Program – Literacy and Numeracy (NAPLAN) and the Higher School Certificate (HSC). Students will engage with the Quality Teaching model to design intellectually rich, meaningful learning experiences. The course also introduces key traditions of educational research from local, regional, and global perspectives, enabling students to critically evaluate and apply research to practice. Through critical reflection and practical application, students will strengthen their curriculum leadership.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate educational research traditions to inform teaching and learning in a new subject area
Construct sophisticated curriculum plans and assessment strategies informed by relevant educational frameworks and policy contexts.
Apply the Quality Teaching model to develop intellectually rich and inclusive learning experiences
Synthesise research evidence to create responsive, evidence-informed teaching programs

title: Cultural Variations in Language Learning
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Many of the cultural expectations that are implicit to language learning are carried subconsciously by native speakers but are often invisible to second language learners. Such aspects as pragmatics, language use, and appropriate role behaviour are often culture-specific and are likely to override semantic considerations for language learners.
learning_outcomes: Identify and describe cultural variations in language usage in both first and second languages;
Identify the cultural elements in language form in both first and second languages;
Design ways of overcoming cultural variation in pedagogical situations; and
Explain and justify cultural standpoints on specific issues of cultural differences.

title: Tesol Curriculum and Methodology
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Develops understanding of curriculum theories and its application in ESL/EFL Syllabus design and ESL/EFL program writing in schools and universities. The pedagogic principles and practices of ESL/EFL teaching will be discussed in relation to curriculum development. It also aims to develop students' understanding of the importance of curriculum innovation in accordance with the global, national and local educational contexts in the 21st century.
learning_outcomes: Discuss and synthesize new directions of teaching English as an international language.
Critically evaluate pedagogical approaches to teaching ESL/EFL;
Design and develop materials and resources to support TESOL;
Apply core knowledge to ESL/EFL syllabus design and ESL/EFL program writing;
Understand and analyse key concepts of curriculum theory and its application;

assessment_tasks.task_name: Essays/Written Assignments (report of a case study)

title: Minor Thesis A
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Provides the opportunity to undertake research in an area of interest to the student. The research may take the form of an empirical study, a review of the literature or another research format in discussion with the supervisor. Taken in conjunction with EDUC6027 Minor Thesis B.
learning_outcomes: To understand the process of research; and
To undertake a research study.

title: Minor Thesis B
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Provides an opportunity to undertake research in an area of interest to the student. The research may take the format of an empirical study, a review of literature or another research format in discussion with the supervisor. Taken in conjunction with EDUC6026 Minor Thesis A.
learning_outcomes: To understand the process of research.
To undertake a research study.

title: Educational Leadership for Digital Learning
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course examines the relationship between digital learning, contemporary ethical governance of technology, and educational leadership. It aims to provide students with the opportunity to explore ethical, governance and planning approaches to integrating educational technology into authentic learning contexts. Students will be given the opportunity to develop and understanding of, and skills in, leading digital learning within relevant educational systems.
learning_outcomes: Make appropriate decisions regarding the selection, integration and ongoing governance of digital learning technology;
Critically examine the impact of digital technology on educational leadership practice;
Plan for appropriate management of digital learning technology;
Use evidence in leadership planning for digital technology planning and governance.
Devise strategies for managing opportunities and risks for the effective implementation of digital learning technology;
Explain ethical models and reasoning for technology integration in educational contexts.
Translate theories and research findings regarding ethics and governance into practice;

title: Power and Pedagogy
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Examines such topics as space and architecture, the organisation of time, documents and artefacts of schooling, school regulations and rituals, classroom practices, and the effects of power on both teachers and students. Students will have the opportunity to apply key concepts of the topic, such as techniques of power, the circulation of power, and power's productiveness, to their own work or educational contexts.
learning_outcomes: Extend students' understanding of power and its relationship to pedagogy in schools and other educational settings
Provide students with conceptual tools to reflect upon current power relations in schooling and educational policy contexts
Challenge students to apply theories of power to analyse its dynamics in educational contexts

assessment_tasks.task_name: Analysis of theories of pedagogy with a professional reflection
Analysis of theories of power with a professional reflection
Applying theories of pedagogy and power

title: Technology Ethics, Policy and Regulation
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Provides an introduction to the main usage of ICT in education. It is designed to introduce students to the various types of ICT usage frameworks, and examine the ways in which ICT can be used to support and extend student learning. Attention is also given to the integration of theory and practice, in particular, the application of research findings to ICT usage in education.
learning_outcomes: Gain a broad overview of the use of ICT;
Understand the place of ICT in modern educational contexts; and
Apply Instructional design models in relation to ICT to educational contexts.

title: Research Methodology
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Provides an introduction to research methodologies in education, both qualitative and quantitative. The subject introduces students to contemporary perspectives in educational research, and in particular focuses on developing a range of skills involved in formulating a research proposal; including framing research questions, reviewing the literature and choosing appropriate methodologies for different types of study. The ways in which researchers from different research traditions use the different methods of collecting research data (for example, interview, questionnaire and observation) will be included. As the subject is intended to prepare students either for a research thesis or an industry-based project, some preliminary work on the development and administration of a research instrument (e.g., a questionnaire or an interview) is included.
learning_outcomes: Formulate and evaluate research questions
Search for, select and critically analyse research articles and papers
Gain experience with instrument development and data collection methods
Develop a research proposal or industry project plan
Understand research ethics for proposal development
Prepare a literature review

title: Leading Technological Integration
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the opportunity to explore ways in which digital technology can be integrated across the curriculum. Students will be given the opportunity to develop knowledge and skills in the use of ICT technologies within authentic teaching and learning contexts.
learning_outcomes: Develop an understanding of technology integration for education in diverse contexts.
Understand the digital learning needs of diverse students in modern educational contexts;
Gain an understanding of the educational use of digital technologies in a range of context areas;
Gain an understanding cross-curriculum technology integration for digital learning;

assessment_tasks.task_name: Presentation followed by question and answer with supporting document provided.

title: Educational Research Methodology 2: Qualitative
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Provides a generic introduction to the knowledge, skills and tools that a student will require when undertaking a qualitative research study in education. In particular, the subject focuses on the areas of data collection and analysis. Emphasis is given to understanding, evaluating, and gaining experience in the multiple processes of gathering, managing, exploring, interrogating and interpreting textual data. This will include practical sessions in using and evaluating Qualitative Data Analysis Software. Students will be encouraged to apply their skills to data that is relevant to their particular specialist needs.
learning_outcomes: To gain knowledge and skills in gathering and analysing educational research data obtained through qualitative methods
To gain knowledge and skills in presenting and evaluating qualitative research findings
To gain knowledge and skills in managing a qualitative research project
To gain knowledge and skills in qualitative research design, and methods
To gain a knowledge of sound research practice across a range of qualitative traditions

title: Educational Research Methodology 1: Quantitative
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Offers students skill development in quantitative methods of the collection, analysis and reporting of research data, including introduction to the statistical software package SPSS. Analyses of data and hypothesis testing are undertaken using basic descriptive and inferential statistical procedures.
learning_outcomes: Interpret the results of analysis and write reports of results.
Describe and analyse group data using the statistical package SPSS.
Determine an appropriate method of analysis.
Decide an appropriate approach to and method of data collection.

title: Industry/Work Based Project
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Conducted in a workplace or industry educational setting, the course will provide students with the opportunity to design, conduct and analyse research focusing on an issue of concern to them in an in-depth manner.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the role of research in guiding policy and practice
Demonstrate research planning, implementation and analysis skills
Demonstrate conceptual level understanding of their chosen workplace or industry problem.

title: Introduction to Hearing, Audiology, and Assistive Listening Technology
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide teachers with an overview of hearing, audiology and assistive listening technology for children and students who are deaf or hard of hearing. Participants will be introduced to the anatomy and physiology of hearing as a basis for understanding the mechanisms underlying auditory perception. The causes and implications of various types of hearing loss including temporary hearing loss associated with otitis media in indigenous children will be examined. Procedures and testing techniques will also be explored. Topics covered will include screening, behavioural assessment, objective assessment, and evoked potential testing techniques. Students will develop an understanding of clinical reports and audiograms. Hearing aids, cochlear implants and other assistive listening devices are reviewed. Students will learn skills in troubleshooting and monitoring such devices in a 1-day workshop.
learning_outcomes: Explain the delivery of audiology services for children and students with hearing loss;
Discuss the underlying theory and practical application of environmental acoustics and modifications, and to apply this to school-based settings and Indigenous, home or community settings.
Identify and describe audiological screening and assessment procedures;
Describe the components and features of hearing aids, cochlear implants and FM systems; and
Independently interpret and transmit audiology terminology and constructs with parents of children with hearing loss;
Demonstrate an understanding of how to independently identify, locate and critically evaluate evidence about hearing, audiology, and assistive listening technology.

title: Understanding How Students Who are Deaf or Hard of Hearing Learn
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to the historical, social, cultural and political contexts of educating children and young people who are deaf or hard of hearing. It provides an overview of deaf education and early intervention settings and services at local, national and international levels; reviews political, legislative and professional contexts of deaf education; and identifies reasonable adjustments for students who are deaf or hard of hearing. Family-centred early intervention and education is identified from a theoretical and practical perspective with an additional focus on Indigenous children with otitis media.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced knowledge and understanding of the impact of culture, cultural identity and linguistic background on the education of students from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander backgrounds;
Demonstrate advanced knowledge of teaching strategies that are responsive to the learning strengths and needs of students from diverse linguistic, cultural, religious and socioeconomic backgrounds;
Understand the relevant legislative, administrative and organisational policies and processes required for teachers according to school stage; and
Demonstrate advanced knowledge and understanding of legislative requirements and teaching strategies that support participation and learning of students with disability;
Demonstrate advanced knowledge and understanding of the social historical aspect of people who are deaf and hard of hearing;
Understand strategies for working effectively, sensitively and confidentially with children with disabilities and their families.
Demonstrate advanced knowledge and understanding of physical, social and intellectual development and characteristics of students and how these may influence learning;
Demonstrate advanced knowledge of, understanding of and respect for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander histories, cultures and languages and the associated influence of hearing loss;
Demonstrate advanced knowledge and understanding of research into how students learn and the implications for teaching;

title: Speech and Children who are Deaf or Hard of Hearing
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course presents an analysis and synthesis of concepts and theories relating to speech development, assessment and remediation of children who are deaf or hard of hearing. Typical speech perception and the continuum of development supporting the emergence of mature speech production is critically analysed. Students will interpret theoretical propositions and apply established theories and strategies to assess and enhance the intelligibility of speech for listeners who are deaf or hard of hearing.
learning_outcomes: Apply the physics of sound including frequency, amplitude, resonance and associated theories;
Explain the typical course of vocal development leading to intelligible speech production;
Demonstrate an advanced understanding of assessment strategies, including informal and formal, diagnostic, formative and summative approaches to assess student learning;
Broadly describe the continuum of phonological and articulation development in young children;
Apply the physics of sound to an audiogram;
Demonstrate competence in reporting assessment results and establishing short and long term speech goals;
Demonstrate advanced knowledge of a range of strategies and programs designed to facilitate/remediate speech development; and
Demonstrate advanced knowledge of, and the capacity to access, current professional literature in speech development and assessment in children and adolescents with hearing loss.

title: Language and Literacy of Children Who are Deaf or Hard of Hearing
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course explores the relationship between language and literacy development and the impact of hearing loss on the child's acquisition of both language and literacy skills. The content covers the structure and function of language, theoretical frameworks related to first language acquisition, language development milestones, and concepts and principles of literacy development.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an advanced understanding of how speaking, listening, reading, writing and thinking are interrelated and developmental processes;
Demonstrate advanced understanding of assessment strategies, including informal and formal, diagnostic, formative and summative approaches to assess student learning;
Demonstrate advanced capacity to interpret student assessment data to evaluate student learning and modify teaching practice.
Demonstrate an understanding of how to independently identify, locate and critically evaluate evidence pertaining to the above-listed outcomes
Identify and administer appropriate language and literacy assessment for children with hearing loss;
Describe the typical development of language and communication and the impact of hearing loss;
Demonstrate advanced understanding of assessment moderation and its application to support consistent and comparable judgements of student learning;

title: Assessment, Programming and Intervention in Behaviour Problems
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Explores the importance of a sound approach to implementing any behaviour change program. The need for adequate and appropriate data gathering as a basis for planning a behaviour support procedure will be examined, followed by systematic implementation with both ongoing and review evaluation. The course is based on a programming model of assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation.
learning_outcomes: develop knowledge of the contextual factors in identifying and assessing behaviour needs
demonstrate knowledge of, and ability to implement, alternate intervention approaches for problem behaviour
conduct a behavioural functional assessment that leads to informed intervention procedures
examine issues involved in assessment, programming and implementation in the field of emotional disturbance and behaviour disorders

title: Whole School Approaches to Supporting Student Behaviour
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Introduces the range of approaches to managing student behaviour including what a whole-school approach is; the Effective Behaviour Support Model; the importance of whole school approaches in the context of the home, school and community; and whole school approaches such as discipline and restitution models and their implementation.
learning_outcomes: understand their local school community and the use of both student and staff development resources
locate various electronic resources on whole school approaches
describe a whole school behaviour model and its application in schools.
explain why whole school approaches in managing problem behaviour is effective
recognise the link between whole school approaches, home, school and community issues.

title: Practicum for Teachers of Children Who are Deaf or Hard of Hearing
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Qualified teacher wishing to specialise in Deaf Studies and Deaf Education within the Master of Special and Inclusive Education programme must complete a practicum. Depending on the relevant regulatory authority’s accreditation requirements, the length of the practicum will vary. For most students, the practicum will be 20 days. Victorian DET Scholarship students enrolled in the Master of Special and Inclusive Education are required to complete a 30-day practicum.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced knowledge and understanding of strategies for differentiating teaching to meet the specific learning needs of students across the full range of abilities;
Use curriculum, assessment and reporting knowledge to design learning sequences and lesson plans;
Organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence;
Demonstrate an advanced capacity to interpret student assessment data to evaluate student learning and modify teaching practice.
Demonstrate advanced knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content and teaching strategies of the teaching area;
Plan lesson sequences using knowledge of student learning, content and effective teaching strategies;
Demonstrate understanding of applied literacy teaching strategies and their application in teaching areas;
Set learning goals that provide achievable challenges for students of varying abilities and characteristics;

title: Policy, Administration and Collaboration in Special and Inclusive Education
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course examines collaboration, consultation, negotiation, and interdisciplinary teams related to children and young people with disability, their families and allied health practitioners. The course examines policy development and application; curriculum and personalised learning; and the ability of the workforce to meet the needs of children and young people with disability in education settings. The course also reviews related professional ethics requirements and challenges. The course includes an in-depth discussion of legislation prohibiting discrimination in education settings. The course highlights the various global perspectives of the endeavour to collect data on children and young people with disability.
learning_outcomes: Apply negotiation and conflict resolution theory and practice in education settings; and
Describe and engage with interdisciplinary teams
Assess inclusive education workforce capability
Express an understanding of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and Disability
Describe effective collaboration and consultation in education settings
Express an understanding of governmental disability planning and the various global perspectives on the rights of persons with disability
Explain policy development and implementation in education settings
Evaluate professional ethics

title: Using Resources in Behaviour Problems
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Introduces the range of approaches to managing individual student behaviour needs including evaluating individual behaviour plans, dealing with comorbid behaviours, and addressing academic and social needs.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and review effective positive behaviour programs and determine their validity through the investigation of behaviour literature
Examine both human and material resources involved in the provision of quality interventions and settings in the field of emotional disturbance and behaviour disorders

Examine both human and material resources involved in the provision of quality interventions in the field of emotional disturbance and behaviour disorders; and to be able to evaluate effective positive behaviour programs.

Discuss and develop alternate approaches to managing and self-management of behaviour through investigation of direct instruction, cognitive, metacognitive, cooperative learning methods and social skills

title: Education of Students with Learning Difficulties
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Course participants will acquire knowledge of research-based practice related to the education of students with additional needs, with a focus on learning difficulties in the academic areas of reading, spelling, mathematics and comprehension. An overview is provided of likely causes of learning difficulties or the effects of these difficulties on reading, spelling or numeracy. Methods of assisting children with learning difficulties are also reviewed, how to plan and implement clearly structured and sequenced teaching activities that scaffold learning for individual students. inclusive of using teaching strategies based on knowledge of students’ physical, social and intellectual development and characteristics to improve student learning for some of our most vulnerable learners
learning_outcomes: Provide an overview of current evidence and research identifying likely causes of learning difficulties
Outline the nature of the reading process and identify the likely effects of underlying causes on specific reading skills and strategies

Provide information of the nature of specific difficulties in spelling, writing and numeracy and how to plan and implement clearly structured and sequenced teaching activities that scaffold learning for individual students with learning difficulties
Discuss methods of identification of underlying causes of learning difficulties

Provide an overview of service delivery models for studies with learning difficulties inclusive of selecting and using a flexible and effective repertoire of teaching strategies to meet the needs, capacities and interests of individual students.

title: Introduction to Challenging Behaviour and Positive Support
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Examines contemporary theory and research of behaviour management in classrooms from minor unproductive behaviour to more challenging behaviour. The content will cover an exploration of challenging behaviours, introducing approaches such as preventative positive behaviour for learning support and self-regulation strategies to address these behaviours.
learning_outcomes: Observe and identify challenging behaviours in the classroom;
Identify, observe and critique current practices and research literature in managing challenging behaviours in the classroom and specialist settings;
Demonstrate knowledge and understand of identification, assessment and the implementation of strategies to address challenging behaviours.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the theory and research of classroom management that conceptualises challenging behaviour;

title: Educating Students with Developmental Diversity
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course develops students’ understanding of the factors involved in diverse learners' experiences in childhood development. It focuses on individuals with physical, cognitive or emotional differences and abilities, as well as differences created by social and ecological factors. Approaches to learning for children with delayed development, gifted and talented, emotional or behavioural issues are examined.
learning_outcomes: Use critical reflection practices to evaluate personal philosophical underpinnings used in support of students with developmental diversity
Explain how individual differences can be created by linking ecological factors with the related diversity
Apply knowledge of how to design educational and support strategies across individual differences in classroom settings
Apply the policies and legislation governing the identification of developmental diversity in relation with specific student characteristics
Demonstrate an understanding of children's developmental and individual learning abilities through an evaluation of the role and relationship of diagnoses and classification systems

title: Pedagogical Innovation with Technologies
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the opportunity to explore ways in which emerging digital technologies can be transformative in terms of student learning. Students will also be given the opportunity to develop understanding and skills in the use of these technologies within teaching and learning contexts.
learning_outcomes: Develop meaningful learning experiences that utilize emerging technologies in effective ways.
Understand the digital learning needs of students in modern educational contexts; and
Gain an understanding of learning in relation to emerging digital technologies;
Gain an overview of educational trends and uses of specific emerging technologies for education;

assessment_tasks.task_name: Analysis of an emerging technology in a specific educational context
Presentation followed by question and answer with supporting document provided

title: Teaching Methods and Techniques in Special and Inclusive Education
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Course participants will engage in learning to enhance knowledge and practice of research-based evidence related to the range of instructional strategies available to educators working with students with additional needs and/or disability. Issues considered include the translation of research into practice, the relationship of emerging approaches to inclusion inclusive of planning and implementing clearly structured and sequenced teaching activities that scaffold learning for students with additional needs and/or disability in individualized, small and large group instruction that are responsive to their learning strengths and needs, and the contribution of efficacy studies to the field.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the theoretical basis for and current research directions around the demonstrated evidence-based practice or teaching strategy used in special education and related fields, and the concomitant relationships between theory and practice, especially in the selections and implementation of effective teaching strategies for students with complex needs.

Evaluate the role and impact of secondary variables that influence program delivery in special and inclusive education, such as inclusion policies and resourcing issues, when planning and implementing structured and sequenced teaching programs that scaffold learning for individual students with additional needs and/or disabilities.

Explore the theory, research and implementation of a range of teaching approaches used in special and inclusive education, in the context of other variables such as educational settings, student's physical, social and intellectual development and characteristics, resourcing issues and emerging policy directions in the area.

title: Mathematics Curriculum Studies 1
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to the key concepts underlying a deep understanding of algebra, functions, continuity and an introduction to calculus. This course will consider the historical development of calculus and will examine current related pedagogical models within the field of secondary mathematics.
learning_outcomes: Design effective lesson plans that incorporate these mathematical concepts, aligning with curriculum standards and addressing diverse learner needs.
Implement a range of strategies for teaching secondary mathematics, tailored to varied classroom contexts.
Demonstrate mastery of key concepts related to fundamental algebra, functions, continuity, and calculus.

title: Mathematics Curriculum Studies 2
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to the key concepts underlying a deep understanding of number, arrangements, number distribution and combinatorics. This course will consider the historical development of number and will examine current related pedagogical models within the field of secondary mathematics, including assessment policy and structure.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate mastery of key concepts related to number theory, combinatorics, the binomial theorem and complex numbers;
Apply a range of strategies for assessing students learning.
Design effective lesson experiences that incorporate the knowledge and beliefs that learners bring to a learning task;

title: Mathematics Curriculum Studies 3
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to the key concepts underlying a deep understanding of mathematical proof and topology. This course will consider the historical development of mathematical proof and topology and will examine current related pedagogical models within the field of secondary mathematics including catering for differentiated learning needs in the contemporary classroom.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate mastery of key concepts related to various forms of mathematical proof and the fields of discrete mathematics and topology;
Design effective lesson plans aligning with curriculum standards.
Apply differentiated learning strategies to the design of lessons in mathematics.

title: Mathematics Curriculum Studies 5
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to the key concepts underlying statistical methods of data analysis and probability leading to an appreciation of variability and related distributions of measure. The course will also examine current related pedagogical models within the field of secondary mathematics including communicating with students and parents.
learning_outcomes: Design and evaluate appropriate statistical methods to communicate educational outcomes
Create a group learning experience (lessons and assessment) using ICT
Demonstrate mastery of key concepts related to methods of data collection, analysis and display;

assessment_tasks.task_name: Assignment - Statistical Significance and Survey Design

title: Mathematics Curriculum Studies 4
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to the key concepts underlying measurement and trigonometry. This course will consider the historical development of trigonometry and other measurement related topics and will examine current related pedagogical models within the field of secondary mathematics, including methods of communicating mathematical reasoning.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate mastery of key concepts related to measurement and trigonometry from a mathematical perspective;
Apply disciplinary communication skills to explain mathematical reasoning.
Design assessment task related to these topics that incorporate use of ICT;

title: Mathematics Curriculum Studies 6
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course will extend students' understanding of calculus and related applications. The course will examine topics such as ordinary differential equations, multiple integrals, limits and continuity, and real or complex variable analysis. The course will also examine current related pedagogical models within the field of secondary mathematics.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate mastery of concepts related to calculus (analysis) involving topics such as ordinary differential equations, multiple integrals, limits and continuity, real or complex variable analysis;
Justify how the unit addresses common misconceptions that students may have about the mathematical content covered.
Design a Unit plan incorporating key elements of the NSW Quality Teaching Model; and

title: Integrated Fieldwork Studies
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: EDUC6109 Integrated Fieldwork Studies provides participants with an opportunity to explore and/or expand their specialisation in school, early childhood, or special education settings. Participants are required to complete a practicum experience relevant to their specialisation and critically reflect on their professional experience in the school context, giving consideration to their professional (in most cases, teaching) philosophy. For course participants in the Masters of Education (Teacher Retraining Stream), and the Masters of Special and Inclusive Education, depending on the relevant regulatory authorities’ accreditation requirements, the length of the practicum will vary: - For most students, the practicum will be 15 days. - Victorian DET Scholarship students enrolled in the Master of Special and Inclusive Education are required to complete 30 days of practicum. This will be broken into two 15 day phases, with one placement in a special education setting and one phase in an inclusive (mainstream) setting (* see note below on the definition of an ‘inclusive setting’ for the purposes of this course). For course participants in the Master of Applied Linguistics: - The NSW Department of Education will recognise graduates of the Master of Applied Linguistics as an English as a Second Language Teacher, where they have also completed an accredited teaching degree and have been registered as teachers with the NSW Education Standards Authority (NESA). - Qualified teachers who wish to gain accreditation as an English as a Second Language Teacher must: complete EDUC6109 Integrated Fieldwork Studies and 40 units of Directed courses in their program of study. - EDUC6109 must be taken in the final term of study. - For recognition in other states and territories, graduates should contact the Department of Education in the relevant jurisdiction to determine the specific requirements for recognition as an English as a Second Language Teacher.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of their ethical behaviour contextualised in their professional standards and articulate a professional philosophy relevant to their specialisation

Depending on specialisation, deliver a series of lessons, activities or interventions within a mainstream (and/or inclusive) school, early childhood or special setting that meets the needs of a variety of students
Critically reflect on professional practice with consideration given to models of learning and professional standards frameworks
Apply concepts and methods related to models of teaching and learning such as the Quality Teaching Model, Response to Intervention or Universal Design for Learning

title: Introduction to Strategic Leadership
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course is intended to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of leadership principles and practices. It focuses on knowing and developing strategic management, strategic planning, ethical and moral demands, and effective leadership dispositions.
learning_outcomes: Assess exemplary personal leadership styles including values, dispositions, supervisory beliefs and leadership goals;
Synthesize substantial organisational and micro-political understandings including conflict resolution and personnel development;
Evaluate personal leadership capacity and identify processes and practices to further develop new knowledge related to one's leadership capacity.

title: Leading for Learning
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: Students will examine teaching and learning through the lens of transformational leadership. Additionally, the course will focus on the development of learning-focused organisations. Emphasis will be placed on research-informed options for: effective teaching, student engagement and management, program evaluation, real-time reflection, building a cultural of professional renewal and embedding adult learning theory. This course is aptly designed for students who aspire to be leaders in educational settings or other settings where continuous learning is valued and expected.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate current learning organisations in terms of teaching and learning practices and policies using the new knowledge from this course and pose research-based improvements.
Design and support expert professional development systems focused on learning;
Assess the substantial characteristics of high-quality teaching and learning;

title: Research and School Transformation
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This is a research course designed to explore current educational issues in local, national and international contexts. Further, this course is intended to develop a community of learners, leaders and scholars who embed research-informed practice in their schools and/or organisations.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate substantial contemporary regional, national and global issues affecting education;
Create and conduct substantial field research within local education contexts;
Construct new expert knowledge with a community of scholars focused on developing high quality educational learning environments.

title: Introduction to High-Quality Learning Environments
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course focuses on understanding the characteristics of, and building the skills to develop, high quality learning environments; enhancing personnel capacity building; fostering physical and mental health; improving organisational structures; improving group dynamics and modelling positive leadership.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the characteristics of high-quality learning environments and facilitate the development of those characteristics;
Design new knowledge to evaluate educational organisations with a focus on personnel well-being and physical space.
Assess the organisational benefits of a healthy workforce and facilitate the development of personnel including physical and mental wellbeing using this new knowledge;

title: English for Special Purposes
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course develops student understanding of the different styles and contents of English used for commercial, professional and educational purposes as well as skills such as needs analysis and the designing of special curriculum to meet these needs.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the origins of language for special purpose;
Analyse different linguistic features of ESL based on different purposes; and
Discuss implications in curriculum design and teaching methods

title: Supervision, Coaching and Mentoring
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: While many school teachers engage in supervision or mentoring of student teachers and other teachers, few have any training in these practices. This course will provide students with the opportunity to examine their own supervisory, coaching and/or mentoring practice grounded in a strong theoretical and practical basis.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of a range of theoretical and practical approaches to supervision, coaching and mentoring, including approaches to supporting equity and diversity, induction, pedagogy, and school change.
Demonstrate broad knowledge of the philosophical, political and knowledge bases upon which supervision coaching, and mentoring practice rests.
Critically engage with a range of issues and debates that characterise supervision, coaching, mentoring research and practice.

title: Supporting Communication Skills
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with knowledge about typical and atypical language development including the pre-intentional and intentional non-verbal communication stages. As well as developing knowledge of strategies to promote receptive and expressive language skills, the course also addresses the use of augmentative and alternative communication systems to support the social, linguistic and cognitive development of children who may be at risk for being unintelligible or non-speaking.
learning_outcomes: Have knowledge of the purposes for and types of augmentative and alternative communication systems
Have skills in identifying and responding to pre-intentional and early intentional communication and in extending expressive and receptive language skills
Have knowledge and skills to support children's social interactions with typically developing peers
Have knowledge of typical and atypical language development as well as pre-intentional and early intentional communication stages
Have skills in implementing augmentative and alternative communication systems

assessment_tasks.task_name: Case scenario/PBL Exercises: Increasing communication skills

title: Language and Cultural Diversity
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course explores the dynamic interplay between language, culture, and identity, providing first-hand insights into the real-world challenges and responsibilities of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL) (also known as English as an Additional Language/Dialect or EAL/D) professionals. Strengths-based approaches to languages education will be explored using a translanguaging lens. Concepts of culture and Intercultural Communicative Competence (ICC) will be critiqued, and the implications of `world Englishes' for the classroom will be discussed. The course will also consider the cultural diversity inherent to the English as an Additional Language / Dialect (EAL/D) student population, examining issues pertinent to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander learners, students with refugee, asylum seeker, and migrant backgrounds, international students, and `Generation 1.5' learners. Practical strategies for helping learners engage critically with cultural content across the curriculum, and a range of approaches for enhancing cultural and linguistic inclusivity in schools, will also be explored.
learning_outcomes: Identify how culture can influence language attitudes, learning approaches, classroom communication, and assessment practices

Differentiate language instruction to support a range of student cohorts, such as multilingual, migrant, refugee, and asylum seeker background learners, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander learners, and international students
Create and evaluate specialised digital learning resources that utilise a translanguaging approach to scaffold learner engagement with language across the curriculum
Critique models of culture, culturally responsive education, and intercultural competence

assessment_tasks.task_name: Critical Analysis of Curriculum, Assessment, and Teaching Materials
Language Learner Profile and Targeted Learning Plan
Digital Resource Design and Teacher Commentary

title: Contemporary Issues in Early Childhood Intervention
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course explores contemporary and popularised issues that are prevalent in the fields of both inclusive preschool education and early intervention services for infants and young children with disabilities. It seeks to provide knowledge and understanding of emerging evidence-based practices.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of historical factors on contemporary practice in Early Childhood special education
Critique theories, philosophies and curriculum approaches in Early Childhood special education
Describe and critically analyse contemporary issues and trends in Early Childhood special education

assessment_tasks.task_name: On-Line Group Discussion Board Contribution and Presentation

title: Social-Emotional Learning and Positive Behaviour Support for Children 0-5 years
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course provides knowledge about the typical stages of young children's social and emotional development and about the functions underlying challenging behaviour. The course will equip students with the skills to interpret children's behaviour in the context of their environments as well as their cognitive, social and emotional development and to develop responsive strategies to support children's positive behaviour and the acquisition of social and emotional skills.
learning_outcomes: Be able to develop appropriate inclusive and individualized strategies to support positive behaviour in young children
Have knowledge and skills to support children's acquisition of social and emotional skills through both universal and preventive strategies and through intensive individualised programs
Understand typical and atypical socio-emotional development from birth to age 5 years
Have skills to observe, assess and interpret the functions of challenging behaviour, and;

assessment_tasks.task_name: On-Line Group Discussion Board Contribution and Participation - Discussion Questions

title: Collaborative and Inter-disciplinary Approaches in Early Childhood Intervention
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with knowledge about the needs of families of children with disabilities as well as the roles of professionals working with children with disabilities and their families. The focus is on understanding family perspectives and implementing a family-centred approach to early intervention. Students will examine the development of effective parent/professional relationships and consider their application in relation to assessment and the development and implementation of Family Service Plans and Individual Education Plans.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the impact of disability on family life
Have knowledge of effective inter-personal skills for developing and maintaining productive collaborative partnerships
Have skills that support the empowerment of parents of children with disabilities or additional needs
Understand the legal and philosophical bases for providing family-centred and interdisciplinary services to infants and young children with disabilities.
Have knowledge of the factors that may inhibit or enhance the implementation of effective interdisciplinary and family-centred approaches to early childhood intervention

assessment_tasks.task_name: On-Line Discussion Board Contribution and Participation - Reflections and Analysis of Topic Readings

title: Critical Reflections in Special and Inclusive Education Settings
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course provides an investigation of the historical and philosophical underpinnings of inclusive education, offering a comparative analysis of the theories and practices in different classroom contexts. Students will be familiarised with contemporary literature on critical reflection, will apply components of this literature to their work practice, and will compare and contrast examples of critical reflection in a variety of Inclusive, special education and disability service settings with reference to global perspectives in inclusive education.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate theoretical understanding of, and critique (critically reflect upon), current models of inclusive practice in terms of their relevance to particular educational contexts;
Develop personal professional goals and to evaluate the extent of their achievement.
Identify and discuss the principal features of critical reflection in workplace environments;
Apply the important features of critical reflection to a present or past professional experience;

assessment_tasks.task_name: Mission Possible: Your professional Growth Plan

title: Research in Inclusive Education
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: This course introduces key concepts and strategies in both critically analysing and designing robust research in a variety of inclusive, special education and disability service settings. Students will learn to appraise journal articles and other sources, identify the level of rigour in published studies, and how to design studies from a wide range of methodological perspectives.
learning_outcomes: Apply the important features of robust research designs to special or inclusive education.
Identify and discuss the core features of scientifically defensible research;
Justify the importance of research in special and inclusive education;
Recognise and define key terminology associated with quantitative, qualitative, and mix-method research;

assessment_tasks.task_name: Essay: Critical analysis of research and Video Reflection
Design a research proposal and Video Reflection

title: Quality Assessment
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will be introduced to significant literature on dimensions of assessment practice identified in research as contributing to greater and more equitable student achievement. You will have the opportunity to engage in direct analysis of current assessment practice and will acquire a deep working knowledge of how the Quality Teaching Model can enhance your own understanding of assessment practice.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a sophisticated understanding of assessment practice as it relates to pedagogy
Critically analyse current assessment practice
Demonstrate a good understanding of pertinent research literature
Apply the Quality Teaching Model to improve assessment practice
Apply relevant knowledge, skills and critical thinking when using current and emerging tools
Adapt tasks to be both context-sensitive and suitable for the intended audience.

title: Quality Classroom Practice
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
