This course develops the understanding of basic rhythm patterns, the concepts of beat and pulse, the use of various tuned and untuned instruments and how to create a group performance using this media. Introduction to Percussion will develop introductory music reading skills connected with performing a range of repertoire appropriate to this stage.
learning_outcomes: The ability to adapt music making skills to a variety of classroom and extra curricula performance activities.
Aural skills with relation to rhythm, time signature, pitch and performing media.
The ability to select and sequence appropriate repertoire.
Ensemble skills through group performance.
The ability to sight-read a musical rhythm.
The ability to create a simple ensemble performance for tuned and untuned percussion.
Basic concepts of rhythm, beat and pulse.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Assessment 3 - Performance Exam Solo and Ensemble

title: Music Culture and Identity
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: Music and the performing arts are powerful forces that shape cultural identity, artistic expression, and historical change. Students will explore the dynamic relationships between genre, tradition, and technological innovation, gaining a deeper understanding of how these elements have influenced musical practices across different eras and cultures. Through critical listening, contextual analysis, and creative exploration, students will investigate the evolution of sound, texture, and timbre across Western art music, popular music, electronic production, and global traditions. The course also addresses key historical movements, the socio-political forces that have shaped music-making, and the impact of gender, race, and decolonisation on how music is studied, performed, and valued. By engaging with diverse musical perspectives, students will refine their analytical, creative, and technological skills, deepening their ability to critically assess musical works, situate their artistic practice within broader historical narratives, and challenge dominant perspectives in music history and sound studies.
learning_outcomes: Identify historical, cultural, and technological influences on diverse musical traditions.
Analyse musical works through sound, texture, timbre, and socio-political contexts.
Apply critical listening skills to assess aesthetic and structural elements in music.
Evaluate dominant narratives in music history, considering race, gender, and decolonization.
Create research-based insights through creative responses.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Quiz on Music, Identity, and Cultural Context

title: Songwriting
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to the foundational technical skills required to write a song in a contemporary popular style. Students will develop their skills in lyric writing, melodic writing, form, and chord sequences. This course will provide an overview of the use of computer software for recording and presenting works to a professional standard.
learning_outcomes: Identify foundational songwriting techniques in selected musical works
Describe the various stylistic characteristics of popular music and music genres
Create and present a new original work demonstrating foundational songwriting techniques.
Analyse and critique their own works

title: Professional Practice 3
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course further develops skills and knowledge introduced in MUSI1302 for music students in their primary musical practice (which can be an instrument, voice, composition, creative production or music research). Styles and modes of presentation are chosen by each student and may involve technology. Repertoires from diverse styles can be studied such as classical, contemporary, popular, jazz and world music. This course offers students the opportunity for intensive development of their individual skills with a focus on the use of technology in their practice.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to incorporate technology into their practice.

Demonstrate a developed capacity for expression and interpretation as appropriate to their chosen practice, e.g. improvisation, analytical and creative approaches to composition and performance and/or innovative use of technology.
Demonstrate evidence of a practice/work routine and its implementation.

Demonstrate a developed level of implementation of fundamentals of technique applicable to the chosen practice, genres and styles, where appropriate e.g. production standards, control of compositional language, physiological issues and creative use of media.
Continually develop their confidence and positive attitude in presenting work, including preparation, readiness, managing anxiety and engaging with music-makers, audiences and other collaborators.
Demonstrate a developing level of critical thinking and research in the student's work.

title: Ensemble Performance and Musicianship
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: Developing strong ensemble performance skills is essential for musicians seeking to thrive in professional and artistic settings. This course provides students with the opportunity to develop their ensemble performance skills by actively participating in an existing musical ensemble. Through rehearsals, sectionals, and public performances, students will refine their technical proficiency, collaborative musicianship, and interpretative abilities. Students will engage in ensemble-specific repertoire studies, rehearsal techniques, and performance practices while reflecting critically on their role within the group. Ensembles may include orchestras, choirs, jazz bands, contemporary ensembles, chamber groups, electronic music ensembles, or culturally specific music groups. The course also fosters professional skills such as communication, teamwork, stage presence, and repertoire preparation, essential for real-world performance settings.
learning_outcomes: Integrate technical and interpretative proficiency in an ensemble setting.
Critically evaluate ensemble performance practices within historical and cultural contexts.
Demonstrate professionalism, teamwork, and leadership in ensemble environments.
Apply effective rehearsal techniques and ensemble communication strategies.

title: Professional Practice 4
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course further develops skills and knowledge introduced in MUSI2301 for students in their primary musical practices (instrumental or vocal training, composition, studio work and music research). A diverse range of repertoire can be studied such as classical, contemporary commercial, popular, jazz and world music. This course offers the opportunity for the intensive development of individual and collaborative skills using various modes of flexible delivery with a focus on developing an integrated and individual approach to music-making and thinking.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an integrated and fluent understanding of the student's practice/work routine and evidence of its implementation at an increased level of efficiency.
Demonstrate a high level of understanding of critical thinking and research in their work.

Demonstrate an integrated capacity for expression and interpretation as appropriate to their chosen practice (e.g. improvisation, analytical and creative approaches to composition and performance and/or innovative use of technology) and an emergence of individual style.

Demonstrate self-assurance and positive attitude in presenting work, including the ability to listen and be responsive, plus preparation, readiness, managing anxiety and engaging with music-makers, audiences and other collaborators, and managing themselves as a businessperson operating in the music industry.

Demonstrate an integrated and fluent implementation of fundamentals of technique applicable to the chosen practice, genre and style, where appropriate e.g. production standards, control of compositional language, physiological issues and creative use of media.
Demonstrate an ability to communicate specific ideas and needs to collaborators and/or audiences on a professional level.

title: Collaborative Music Making 4
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci

Students will also explore the various ways music is disseminated and promoted in the music industry including live performance and online distribution. Students may explore any music style or genre including contemporary, popular, classical, jazz and folk/world music.

Perform technical work, demonstrating expert control of rhythm, articulation, timbre and intonation
Work effectively in a team within a creative context
Apply expert musicianship through performance

assessment_tasks.task_name: Blog or Wiki Documenting Music Industry Promotion and Engagement Project

title: Collaborative Music Making 3
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This is a practical course in music performance and presentation in collaborative settings. These settings include performances in large and small ensembles (for example orchestra, big band and choir), as well contemporary combinations such as jazz, laptop ensembles and pop bands. It consists of rehearsals and performances in a range of ensembles involving collaborative engagement with other performers, composers and creative producers. Included is the development of skills in music video production for ensembles of varying sizes and make-up. There will also be classes on specific topics relevant to all forms of musical collaboration. Works performed are selected from a wide variety of musical styles and repertoires.
learning_outcomes: Create a live performance event for community engagement.
Perform technical work, demonstrating advanced control of rhythm, articulation, timbre and intonation.
Apply advanced musicianship through performance.
Work effectively in a team within a creative context.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Blog or Wiki Documenting Performance Event Project

title: Creative Music Studio 3
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course extends the fundamentals of music writing by examining music produced for given contexts, such as still or moving image, games, mobile apps and sound installations. Students will consider common forms of music composition/song writing in addition to more experimental processes in composition and production, invoking creativity and experimentation.
learning_outcomes: Identify music written for specific contexts
Complete an experimental music or sound recording
Evaluate the creative aspects of their own composition
Create a piece of music or sound design for a given context

title: Studio Sessions
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course develops students' conceptual and technical skills within the studio environment. Through a combination of practical performance and studio production experiences the course enables opportunity for the development of original material and fosters critical observation and listening.
learning_outcomes: Apply production techniques in the studio environment;
Work effectively in a team within a creative context;
Create a studio based creative work relevant to their area of study.
Analyse performances and identify techniques used to capture them;

title: Chords, Harmonies and Progressions
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course provides the opportunity to creatively apply advanced harmonic techniques in any genre or era as defined by the interest of the student. Examples from a wide diversity of musical styles are presented, including western classical, popular, jazz and world music. This course particularly focuses on the applications of chromatic and extended harmonies that are common across these diverse styles. It also involves analysis and musical problem solving.
learning_outcomes: Create musical harmonic progressions.
Describe harmonic processes used in a variety of musical styles including classical, popular, jazz and world music.
Solve musical harmony problems.
Analyse approaches to musical harmonic organisation.

title: Music Recording and Production Techniques
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course records and mixes music in the professional studio environment. It provides skills and knowledge about audio recording, microphones and miking techniques, mixing and mastering of music as well as developing an understanding of the studio space. You will develop a strong technical capacity through recording music performances and also improve critical listening skills while gaining experience with analog and digital audio technologies.
learning_outcomes: Implement studio practices to capture a multitrack music recording
Develop a professionally mixed and mastered audio work
Apply microphone techniques in a music recording environment
Critically appraise audio material and effectively communicate about recording studio processes and equipment

title: Music Sound and Visual Media
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: Explores the creative and technical aspects, aesthetics, and psychology of combining sound design and music for use with film, video, VR and other visual media. The course examines the interaction of sound and vision in a collaborative creative performance project that combines visual media and original music.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate with co-workers.
Implement technical skills of music creation, synchronisation and editing in creative projects.
Plan and produce a creative project with an intended audio-visual application.
Identify and analyse a range of diverse applications of sound in visual media.
Recognise the terminology and aesthetics associated with film and multimedia production.

title: Songwriting Studio
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course develops students’ songwriting skills for a wide range of musical styles, genres and contexts. Students will extend their songwriting skills in lyric writing, melody writing, form, rhythm, storytelling and harmony. Case studies, critical listening and practical exercises are used as a basis for students creating original compositions produced for industry-based contexts.
learning_outcomes: Identify major songwriting genres and exemplary artists within those genres
Apply knowledge of songwriting copyright and distribution models
Analyse different musical and cultural contexts through songs and their lyrics
Incorporate a variety of performing media and technology in the songwriting process

assessment_tasks.task_name: Songwriting analysis in a professional context

title: Researching Australian Music and the Performing Arts
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course explores Australian music and performing arts. Emerging themes, narratives, and traits will be investigated and challenged through case studies, listening examples, media, and publications. Students will undertake research on Australian music and performance within historical, contemporary, indigenous, and international cultural contexts.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse artistic works, musical scenarios, and underlying principles and concepts prevalent in Australian music;
Examine the cultural contexts of Australian music and performance culture.
Evaluate the historical and contemporary landscape of Australian music and performing arts;

assessment_tasks.task_name: Research Project on Australian Music and the Performing Arts
Sounds of Australia: Annotated Playlist Across Decades

title: Music and Performing Arts Creative Project
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: Bringing a creative vision to life is a vital skill for artists and industry professionals seeking to make a meaningful impact. Students will undertake an individual or collaborative project in a professional or community setting, demonstrating advanced skills in project management, artistic development, and critical reflection. Throughout the course, students will navigate all stages of the creative process—including conceptualisation, planning, execution, presentation, and evaluation—while refining their professional and entrepreneurial capabilities in music and the performing arts.
learning_outcomes: Implement a major creative project in a professional or community setting, demonstrating artistic and technical proficiency.
Evaluate creative projects, incorporating reflective practice and constructive feedback.
Apply creative leadership practices to manage a professional project.
Design a major creative project that demonstrates originality and professional competence.

title: Professional Practice 5
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course further develops skills and knowledge introduced in MUSI2302. It involves advanced music studies for students in their primary musical practices (instrumental or vocal training, composition, studio work and music research). A diverse range of repertoire can be studied such as classical, contemporary commercial music, jazz and world music. This course offers the opportunity of the intensive development of individual and collaborative skills using various modes of flexible delivery with a focus on deepening of stylistic focus and awareness of professional expectations.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an ability to communicate specific ideas and needs to collaborators and/or audiences on a professional level.
Demonstrate advanced ability to think critically and understand the research process in their work.

Demonstrate advanced application of fundamentals of technique applicable to the chosen practice, genre and style where appropriate e.g. production standards, control of compositional language, physiological issues and creative use of media.

Demonstrate advanced level of confidence and self-assuredness in presenting work, including the ability to listen and be responsive, as well as preparation, readiness, managing anxiety; and engaging with music-makers, audiences and other collaborators.

title: Engaging in the Music Industry
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course engages students in the music industry through authentic experiences and projects that prepare them for prospective careers in music. Current digital platforms are discussed with a particular focus on new digital business models, international markets, music streaming and social media. Exploring project pitches and the production process, students will adopt the roles of manager, agent and promoter. Student projects may include, but are not limited to: theoretical explorations and reviews; speculative design practices; professionally oriented projects; work-integrated learning and research-integrated learning opportunities; group / collaborative projects; external stakeholder based projects.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate strategies for marketing and developing audiences
Proficiently navigate the digital platforms relevant to the music industry to promote their area of creative practice
Develop a music industry project proposal from creation to completion

title: Sonic Alchemy: Explorations in Sound and Visualisation
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures

syllabus_overview: This course encourages students to develop new ways of creating within the context of interactivity, music, sound synthesis and visualisation. It cultivates creativity by exploring the generation and processing of music and sound through software and hardware programming. Students investigate current and emerging forms of interactivity in the digital domain through virtual and tactile interfaces.
learning_outcomes: Develop an interactive sound plugin
Reflect on visual and auditory data representations
Generate new sounds through interactive synthesis
Collaborate effectively as a member of a team
Demonstrate techniques for sound visualisation

title: Professional Practice 6
