syllabus_overview: This course brings to culmination all the fundamental music studies, exploration into various genres and developing stylistic focus of previous semesters in the form of a specialist performance/creative or research project. This final semester of the B.Mus. is therefore more open in scope (subject to approval), giving students the opportunity to prepare for a professional career after graduation and possibly Honours.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an ability to focus sophisticated techniques, as applicable, in the realisation of a creative and/or performance project specific to chosen practice.
Demonstrate an understanding of their practice/work routine and evidence of its implementation at an advanced level of efficiency.
Demonstrate the ability to focus critical thinking and the research process in a creative/performance project and/or portfolio.
Demonstrate an ability to communicate via their particular medium at a professional level through diverse means, which may include technology.
Demonstrate evidence of well-developed individual style and highly sensitive expressive control in the realisation of the creative component of the project.
Give a professional presentation at all levels in a performance/creative project or portfolio.

title: Creative Practice Lab
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This practical course is designed to give students a platform to apply their skills and knowledge of performance in a collaborative, interdisciplinary, devised, creative project. It provides an opportunity to apply the knowledge and skills they have accrued to a professional setting and includes possibilities for Work Integrated Learning. This course challenges students to extend their creative potentials and explore artistic boundaries that articulate with professional practices. As part of the self-directed project, students will be required to maintain a critical reflective journal that explains and critiques the project process.
learning_outcomes: Apply creative skills to develop an idea from inception to realisation.
Think critically about devising, realising and producing a collaborative performance project.
Demonstrate advanced understanding of the theoretical background, stylistic details and characteristics of contemporary performance.
Demonstrate professional behaviour and commitment to participating in a collaborative performance project.
Demonstrate the ability to independently manage and present a performance with minimal supervision.

title: Music for Games and VR
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course allows students to engage with the practical technologies and theoretical perspectives that underpin the creation of interactive music for games and virtual reality (VR) environments. It explores the implications of designing sonic content for non-linear media and encourages students to collaboratively engage creatively within this context, using both standard and emerging tools for game and VR music creation.
learning_outcomes: Plan and propose sonic content for game/VR media
Create original sonic content suitable for a game/VR environment
Explain theoretical perspectives on game/VR music design
Interpret and analyse game/VR music design
Integrate sonic content into a game/VR environment
Collaborate effectively as a member of a team

title: Music Research Studies
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to the issues, applications, directions and potentials for music research. Students will develop music research skills through collaboratively workshopping research proposals, reviewing literature and developing projects.
learning_outcomes: Communicate project results in written forms, using academic style.
Identify and critically analyse key issues in music research.
Develop a music research proposal.
Appraise existing literature.

title: Musical Arranging
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: Performers, composers and producers in the 21st century need to be adaptable to different contexts and inventive with their performance and repertoire. This course focuses on arrangement, orchestration, reinterpretation and repertoire creation, using traditional and non-traditional approaches to music and sound making.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate skills in score organisation and analysis.
Rearrange existing repertoire into new contexts.
Apply knowledge of instrumental and vocal characteristics.
Manipulate timbre and/or texture, structure and sound using score and/or technology based processes.
Compare and evaluate stylistic differences.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Major Arrangement with Associated Musical Analysis

title: Music and Health
faculty: College of Human and Social Futures
school: School of Humanities Creative Industries SocialSci
syllabus_overview: Music has been used for centuries to impact mood, movement and behaviour positively. This course combines biological, psychological and sociological approaches to music to explore the ways music interacts with the brain and is used in everyday life. This course examines the different ways music affects us in terms of our emotions, our bodies, and our social connectedness, and how it can be used for positive effects. The approach is across the lifespan, with focuses on childhood, youth and older age, including on dementia. Through establishing criteria for designing an activity, students will also develop critical thinking on the design of music activities in different settings.
learning_outcomes: Analyse ways in which music can be used to alleviate symptoms.
Identify ways in which music can improve health and wellbeing, including mental health.
Explain how music affects emotions, body and social connectedness.
Evaluate the suitability of specific music activities for health purposes.

title: Nutrition 1
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Introduces nutrition and dietetics and education students to the study of nutrition; including nutrients, requirements, food sources and food selection guides. It covers aspects of the Australian Food and Nutrition System (production, distribution, consumption, and food regulation). It also introduces health outcomes and the interpretation of national data related to nutritional conditions, and the research and educational tools used by nutrition professionals.
learning_outcomes: Describe the psychosocial, cultural, political and economic factors influencing food and food use, food habits, diet and lifestyle - food availability and consumption; the role, functions and sources of nutrients; the food selection guides and the dietary guidelines.
Demonstrate practical skills in dietary assessment including recommending solutions to address nutrition issues.
Critically appraise issues in nutrition & dietetics using an evidence-based approach.
Apply current knowledge of the theory of human nutrition and dietetics and related practice, including Nutrient Reference Values and dietary sources and functions of nutrients.

title: Introduction to Dietetics
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course will introduce students to the dietetics profession, as well as the nutrition and dietetics program. Students will learn about the varying roles of dietitians, and the professional activities of successful dietitians. Students will learn and start developing key skills required for dietetic practice, including professional practice skills and collaborative practice skills. Students will be introduced to the concept of expert practice, including evidence-based practice and the Nutrition Care Process.
learning_outcomes: Identify and explain the various roles of dietitians, and the professional activities of successful dietitians
Demonstrate an understanding of expert practice, including evidence-based practice, and the Nutrition Care Process, and how they are applied to dietetic practice.
Demonstrate professional practice skills, including safe and ethical practice, and cultural safety and responsiveness
Demonstrate collaborative practice skills, including communication, working within teams, and identifying collaborators.

title: Community and Public Health Nutrition 1
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Students are introduced to community and public health nutrition practice. A series of lectures and skill based workshops introduce the theory and practice of health promotion and its application to dietetics. As part of this course, students work in teams on a practice based needs assessment project.
learning_outcomes: Define community nutrition/public health nutrition and describe the role of a community dietitian-nutritionist/public health nutritionist.
Demonstrate skills in project management.
Demonstrate skills in written and oral communication.
Demonstrate skills in group work including: - collaboration, teamwork, group negotiation and; - working with other health professionals, stakeholders and partners in a community setting.
Collect, analyse and critically review data examining determinants of nutrition problems in communities/populations to inform development of nutrition programs.
Describe and evaluate methods for examining determinants of nutrition problems in communities/populations to inform development of nutrition programs.

title: Nutrition 2
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Continues on from Nutrition 1 and provides a more in depth examination into the study of essential macronutrients and micronutrients and their recommended intakes, with reference to the Australian diet. The course explores the specific nutritional requirements and nutrition related problems at all stages of the life cycle.
learning_outcomes: Identify vulnerable individual and at-nutritional risk groups according to lifecycle stage
Collect, analyse and assess food intake data

Demonstrate an understanding of nutrition principles and their application to nutritional requirements and Nutrient Reference Values, including issues of deficiency and toxicity, biochemical processes and nutrient interactions
Describe the dietary sources, functions and bioavailability of key nutrients in absorption, metabolism, and assimilation
Critically evaluate current issues and topics in nutrition science by accessing, synthesising and interpreting current literature and resources.

title: Community and Public Health Nutrition 1
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to introduce students to community and public health nutrition practice. A series of lectures and skill-based workshops introduce the theory and practice of health promotion and its application to dietetics, and the nutrition care process. The course will provide students with knowledge and skills in adopting an evidence-based approach to planning community and public health nutrition interventions. The course will also build professional practice skills within community and public health nutrition practice.
learning_outcomes: Describe and evaluate epidemiological methods for examining determinants of nutrition problems in communities/populations to inform development of community and public health nutrition interventions
Demonstrates skills in collaborative practice, including ability to collaborate within a team, and identify opportunities to work with stakeholders in community and public health nutrition practice
Collect, analyse and critically review data examining determinants of nutrition problems in communities/populations to inform development of community and public health nutrition interventions.
Define community nutrition/public health nutrition and describe scope of practice of community dietitians/public health nutritionists

Demonstrate an ability to use a variety of communication methods, to communicate with a range of different audiences within community and public health nutrition, including the translation of research findings
Demonstrates professional practice skills including elements of safe, ethical and legal practice, leadership and, management
Apply best practice frameworks for planning community/public health nutrition interventions

title: Food Science 2
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: An examination of food legislation, chemical, nutritional and microbiological safety factors that influence food production, processing and supply. Special attention will be given to food, health, and culinary nutrition, novel and new foods and food systems.
learning_outcomes: Describe the management of nutritional and food safety aspects in the food industry and food systems.
Participate in collaborative decision making, shared responsibility and shared vision within a team, recognizing the diverse roles other team members play
Demonstrate and apply knowledge of the regulatory and scientific frameworks that control food product information and claims.
Understand the legal framework in food production, processing and supply.
Demonstrate clear and concise written communication, including translating technical information into practical messaging
Applies an evidence-based approach to evaluating the effects of foods and culinary nutrition and their components on human health

title: Dietetic Practice 1
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to upskill students in communication with clients across the Nutrition Care Process, and dietetic practice. The course will provide students with the necessary foundational knowledge and skills to communicate complex concepts to a variety of clients using different methods. Clients include the individuals, groups and populations dietitians communicate with, including patients and their carers, consumers, stakeholders and organisations. Students will apply both nutrition knowledge and behaviour change theory to underpin safe and effective communication with clients. The course will build the professional and communication skills that are foundational to dietetic practice, that will be further developed in the third and fourth year of the program.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate awareness of different methods of communication and how they are used across the Nutrition Care Process, and within dietetic practice.
Demonstrate an ability to translate complex scientific information into a simplified manner to a variety of clients using different communication methods
Demonstrate professional practice skills, including leadership, management and cultural safety and responsiveness
Demonstrate an ability to adapt and create communication messages for specific audiences
Demonstrate collaborative practice skills, including collaborating within a team effectively.
Identify and apply key learning, behaviour change and marketing principles that underpin communication to a variety of clients.

title: Clinical Nutrition 1
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Examines nutrition as it relates to the prevention and treatment of disease. The course deals with the nutritional aspects of diseases and clinical disorders by integrating students' existing knowledge of physiology, biochemistry and food science.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of the Nutrition Care Process and its application to disease prevention, treatment, and management
Demonstrates professional practice skills including safe, ethical, legal and interprofessional practice
Collect, analyse, interpret, and prioritise information related to the health and nutritional status of individuals
Translate evidence-based information to implement, evaluate, and document individualised and practical interventions, and care planning.

title: Dietetic Practice 2
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The learning for this course includes communication skills, dietary intake assessment skills, critical thinking and clinical reasoning skills. The course will also introduce Healthy Conversation Skills, which is a model of health communication that facilitates opportunistic communication with clients in the clinical context. An introduction to the types of strategies that dietitians can use to encourage behaviour change as part of the counselling process will be covered. Students will attend practical placement in a clinical setting and attend skill based workshops to reach professional competency in dietary intake assessment and the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, Nutrition Care Process including writing PES statements, goals, objectives and strategies for change. It is important to note, there will be compulsory clinical and workshop attendances throughout the semester.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrates skills in nutrition diagnosis and selection of an appropriate nutrition intervention for a patient/client, including critical thinking and clinical reasoning skills
Demonstrates reflective practice
Demonstrates skills in client centered counselling
Demonstrates skills in nutrition assessment of patients/clients through interview, observation and measurements
Demonstrates effective verbal and written communication with patients/clients across the nutrition care process
Demonstrates professional practice skills including safe, ethical and legal interprofessional practice, leadership, management, and cultural safety and responsiveness

title: Nutrition Communication
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Students will learn the theory of nutrition education and communication with a key focus on its application to groups in the community. Students will apply both nutrition knowledge and health behaviour change to the process of nutrition education and communication to empower groups and/or the broader community to improve their own health through engagement, facilitation, education and collaboration.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate awareness of different modes of professional communication, and apply active listening, models of behaviour change to nutrition education and communication.
Apply the principles of marketing to promote healthy eating and influence dietary change.
Demonstrate an ability to translate complex/scientific information into a simplified manner for communication to general population.
Display effective active listening, interviewing and interpersonal skills.
Describe the principles of adult education and communication for group processes.
Demonstrate knowledge of communication on a range of platforms including written, verbal and social media/technology.
Demonstrate skills required for successful facilitation and communication of nutrition information, including conflict management.

title: Clinical Nutrition 2
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Studies clinical nutrition as it relates to the prevention and treatment of disease. The course deals with the nutritional aspects of diseases and clinical disorders by integrating students' existing knowledge of physiology and biochemistry and food science.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of the Nutrition Care Process and its application to disease prevention, treatment, and management
Collect, analyse, interpret, and prioritise information related to the health and nutritional status of individuals
Demonstrates professional practice skills including safe, ethical and legal practice, and cultural safety and responsiveness
Translate evidence-based information to implement, evaluate, and document individualised and practical nutrition goals, interventions, and care planning.

title: Food and Nutrition Service Management
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course introduces a systems approach to management concepts and explores issues associated with the management of foodservice operations. This includes menu planning, ordering, preparation methods for quantity food production, quality control, and human resource management within a quality management framework. You will have the opportunity to apply your theoretical knowledge and skills in professional food service practice undertaken in the 4th yr of the program. The concepts that are covered with respect to foodservice will be applied to nutrition services in a general sense. Entry level practitioners require management skills to contribute effectively to the delivery of nutrition services. In addition, many practitioners take on sole positions which usually include management roles, or wish to enter business for themselves. You should therefore find this course, while different from your previous courses, directly relevant to any dietetic position.
learning_outcomes: Develop and modify recipes according to therapeutic diet standards including texture modification in food service settings.
Acting professionally, providing advice and leadership in a food service setting to ensure provision of safe and nutritious food according to professional standards.
Assess and evaluate the operation and management of food services using quality improvement cycles to ensure they are efficient, sustainable and effective.
To demonstrate understanding and explain food service systems and the interconnected relationships between these systems.
To demonstrate understanding and apply nutrition and food standards and guidelines for recipe development, menu planning and menu assessment for groups in food service settings

title: Community and Public Health Nutrition 2
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course builds upon the knowledge and skills obtained in Community and Public Health Nutrition 1. The course will provide students with knowledge and skills in adopting an evidence-based approach to planning, implementation, and evaluation of community and public health nutrition interventions. The course will also build the professional and communication skills relevant to community and public health nutrition practice, and further expand students understanding of the roles and functions of the community and public health nutrition workforce.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an ability to use a variety of communication methods, to communicate with a range of different audiences within community and public health nutrition, including the translation of research findings
Apply best practice frameworks for the planning, implementation and evaluation of community/public health nutrition interventions.
Identify and select appropriate research methods to evaluate community and public health nutrition interventions.
Demonstrates professional practice skills including safe, ethical and legal practice, leadership, management and cultural safety and responsiveness.
Critically appraise nutrition epidemiology and use the best available evidence to inform community and public health nutrition intervention planning and implementation

Demonstrates skills in collaborative practice, including ability to collaborate within a team and identify opportunities to work collaboratively and build capacity with stakeholders in community and public health nutrition practice

title: Professional Practice in Nutrition and Dietetics 1 Part A
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: NUDI4233A and NUDI4233B together comprise 10 weeks of professional practice in community and food service settings, and the telehealth clinic. This course consists of 5 weeks of Community and Public Health Nutrition Placement and 4 weeks of Food Service Placement as well as three telehealth clinics. Students complete the Community and Public Nutrition and Food Service Placements in groups of 2 to 4. There is a transitioning to practice workshop, as well as 1 online session. Student attendance at the workshop is compulsory.
learning_outcomes: Competence in the collection, organisation and assessment of data relating to the health and nutritional status of groups or populations as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia
Knowledge sufficient to support safe practice as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia as they apply to the telehealth clinical setting.
Knowledge sufficient to support safe practice as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia as they apply to the foodservice setting.
An organised, planned, professional and ethical approach to work as per National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia
Knowledge sufficient to support safe practice as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia as they apply to the community and public health nutrition setting.
Competence in the management of projects and programs for groups or populations as per National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia

assessment_tasks.task_name: Professional Practice Porfolio including Assessment of Professional Practice Forms (Individual)

title: Professional Practice in Nutrition and Dietetics 1 Part B
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: NUDI4233A and NUDI4233B together comprise 10 weeks of professional practice in community and food service settings, and the telehealth clinic. This course consists of 5 weeks of Community Placement and 4 weeks of Food Service Placement to a total of 9 weeks placement, as well as three telehealth clinics. Students complete the Community and Public Health Nutrition and Food Service Placements in groups of 2 to 4. There is a Reflections and Future Directions workshop, as well as 1 online session. Student attendance at the workshop is compulsory.
learning_outcomes: Competence in the management of projects and programs for groups or populations as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia
Knowledge sufficient to support safe practice as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia as they apply to the foodservice setting.

Competence in the collection, organisation and assessment of data relating to the health and nutritional status of groups or populations as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia
An organised, planned, professional and ethical approach to work as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia
Knowledge sufficient to support safe practice as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia as they apply to the telehealth clinical setting.
Knowledge sufficient to support safe practice as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia as they apply to the community setting.

title: Professional Practice in Nutrition and Dietetics 2 Part A
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: NUDI4245A and NUDI4245B jointly comprise of 10 weeks of professional practice in the setting across the year. Jointly these courses develop students' dietetic practice competencies to entry level standard in accordance with the professional requirements of the Dietitians Association of Australia. This consists of 10 weeks of clinical placements within a dietetic department. There is a transitioning to practice workshop as well as 1 online session. Student attendance at the workshop is compulsory.
learning_outcomes: An organised, professional and ethical approach to work as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia.
Competence in the management of nutrition care for individuals as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia
Knowledge sufficient to ensure safe practice as per National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia as they apply to the clinical/acute care setting.

Competence in the collection, organisation and assessment of data relating to the health and nutritional status of individuals and groups as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia

title: Professional Practice in Nutrition and Dietetics 2 Part B
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: NUDI4245A and NUDI4245B jointly comprise of 10 weeks of professional placement in the clinical acute care setting across the year. Jointly these courses develop students' dietetic practice competencies to entry level standard in accordance with the professional requirements of the Dietitians Association of Australia. This consists of 10 weeks of clinical placements within a dietetic department. There is a Reflections and Future Directions workshop, as a well as 1 online session. Student attendance at the workshop is compulsory.
learning_outcomes: An organised, professional and ethical approach to work as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia
Competence in the management of nutrition care for individuals as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia

Competence in the collection, organisation and assessment of data relating to the health and nutritional status of individuals and groups as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia
Knowledge sufficient to ensure safe practice as per the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia as they apply to the clinical/acute care setting.

title: Paediatric Nutrition and Dietetics
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course examines the application of nutrition and dietetics knowledge in the field of child and family health and nutrition. The course aims to develop a holistic approach to optimising the nutritional health of this group.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of the Nutrition Care Process and its application to disease prevention and management in babies, children, adolescents.
Collect, organise, and assess information related to the health and nutritional status of babies, children, and adolescents, using the Nutrition Care Process
Demonstrate a professional and autonomous approach to dietetic practice.
Interpret and translate scientific knowledge into practical and patient-centred interventions for babies, children, adolescents, and their families.

title: Sports Dietetics
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Sports Dietetics is the study of nutrition and exercise in promotion of health, and prevention and management of disease process for groups with specific nutrient needs. Applied exercise science is integrated with nutrition and dietetics.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and translate scientific knowledge into practical and patient-centred interventions for athletes
Demonstrate knowledge of the unique nutrient requirements of athletes and nuances across sports and populations
Demonstrate knowledge of the role/scope of practice of sports dietitians
Demonstrate knowledge of the nutrition care process and its application to sports dietetics
Collect, organise, and assess information related to the health and nutritional status of athletes, using the Nutrition Care Process

title: Professional Practice in Nutrition and Dietetics A
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course provides essential preparation for professional practice as a dietitian. Under the supervision of an experienced supervisor, students will be given the opportunity to develop skills and competencies across a variety of nutrition and dietetic workplace settings to entry-level standards in accordance with the professional requirements of Dietitians Australia. This course contributes towards the total 100 days of placement required in accordance with the professional requirements of Dietitians Australia.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate safe, ethical and professional practice in a nutrition and dietetic workplace setting.
Practices collaboratively and communicates respectfully and effectively to improve nutrition and health outcomes.
Critically appraise and use an evidence-informed decision-making approach to solve problems and create realistic solutions in a range of practice environments.
Applies an evidence-based approach to nutrition and dietetic practice and advocates for change to improve nutrition, food standards and the food system

title: Professional Practice in Nutrition and Dietetics B
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course provides essential preparation for professional practice as a dietitian. Under the supervision of an experienced supervisor, students will be given the opportunity to develop skills and competencies across a variety of nutrition and dietetic workplace settings to entry-level standards in accordance with the professional requirements of Dietitians Australia. This course contributes towards the total 100 days of placement required in accordance with the professional requirements of Dietitians Australia.
learning_outcomes: Critically appraise and use an evidence-informed decision-making approach to solve problems and create realistic solutions in a range of practice environments.
Practices collaboratively and communicates respectfully and effectively to improve nutrition and health outcomes.
Applies an evidence-based approach to nutrition and dietetic practice and advocates for change to improve nutrition, food standards and the food system.
Demonstrate safe, ethical and professional practice in a nutrition and dietetics workplace setting

title: Essentials of Professional Communication
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Effective professional communication is an essential requirement for today’s registered nurse caring for the Australian population. This course provides students with the knowledge and principles of interpersonal communication, guiding them to develop verbal, non-verbal and written communication skills in various healthcare contexts. It explores therapeutic and person-centred communication including those with special needs and/or in challenging situations, promoting quality care and patient safety. The course prepares students to communicate with patients, healthcare professionals, academics and peers, providing opportunities to practice communication skills, through case studies informed by the National Health Priority Areas. By the end of the course students will demonstrate knowledge, understanding and skills integral to effective professional communication.
learning_outcomes: Identify appropriate communication strategies for people from different cultures, people with special needs and challenging communication situations
Apply effective intraprofessional and interprofessional communication strategies in simulated healthcare scenarios
Explain how therapeutic communication contributes to the development of safe person-centred nurse-patient relationships
Demonstrate effective communication skills in oral, digital and written communication including fundamental academic literacy skills

title: Introduction to the Profession of Nursing
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course prepares students for the professional standards, expectations and regulatory frameworks associated with the Registered Nurse role in contemporary Australian health care. The course explores current ethical, legal and professional issues in nursing in the context of culturally competent, safe, person-centred care. Students develop knowledge of the principles of care through the application of relevant models and frameworks for nursing practice including the Roper-Logan-Tierney model, the Clinical Reasoning Cycle, the person-centred nursing framework and the reflective practice framework - Situation, Past learning experience, Read and refer, Other internal/external, Understanding, Take it forward (SPROUT). Case studies are used to explore relevant aspects of patient safety including the nursing role in fostering a culture of safety and strategies to promote wellness.
learning_outcomes: Describe models and frameworks for nursing practice relating to the planning and provision of person-centred, transculturally competent care and the development of reflective practice.
Explain the principles of relevant Codes and Standards that underpin the professional conduct expectations and accountability processes governing contemporary nursing practice in Australia.
Describe and apply ethical and legal principles in decision-making.
Identify professional development requirements for nurses in Australia, including strategies for maintaining resilience, capability for practice, wellbeing and adapting to change.
Identify the professional attributes, values, historical and contemporary roles and key concepts which are the foundation for contemporary nursing practice in Australia.

Explain current quality and safety issues in health care including the essential characteristics of and processes that contribute to a culture of safety (including cultural safety) and safe outcomes for patients across a range of settings and contexts (including digital contexts).

title: Evidence for Nursing Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Evidence-based practice is an approach to care that integrates the best available research to inform contemporary practice. This course will provide a foundational overview of evidence-based practice. By the end of this course, students will have an appreciation for the steps in the evidence-based practice process and the contribution that ‘best practice’ makes to quality care and safety. The principles of ‘best practice’ will be explored with respect to relevant examples and contexts of care.
learning_outcomes: Define evidence-based practice and identify the benefits and challenges of using this approach for the delivery of health care.
Identify examples of the integration of evidence using clinical expertise and patient preferences to provide appropriate safe and responsive quality nursing care.
Summarise and appraise evidence and for its validity, impact and applicability to practice.
Develop questions which are relevant to nursing practice and patients' experiences of health care.
Devise search strategies to locate the best available evidence to answer those questions.

title: Essentials of Caring for the Older Person
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course explores the knowledge and principles of care in relation to healthy ageing and issues, challenges and supports for older people in Australia. Students will gain an understanding of the importance of promoting quality of life, independence and maintaining choice and dignity for older people as they live with age-related changes, risk factors, sociocultural issues and functional consequences. A focus of this course is to develop student knowledge and skills for the provision of person-centred, evidence-based nursing care for the older person across a range of health settings. Students will understand the complexity of local, national and global issues related to caring for older person.
learning_outcomes: Explain the concept of healthy ageing and its promotion at an individual and community level.
Describe relevant social, political, legal and ethical implications of ageing across local, national and global contexts.
Relate the Quality Use of Medicines framework to the essentials of caring for the older person.
Apply the Roper-Logan-Tierney Model of Nursing and the Clinical Reasoning Cycle to the holistic and comprehensive assessment and planning of care for the older person.

title: Professional Experience 1
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course provides opportunities for students to consolidate theoretical knowledge, acquire skills and apply principles of care through case studies informed by the National Health Priority Areas. Within the simulated learning environment (SLE), skill acquisition and rehearsal take place using clinical reasoning with application to authentic simulated patient scenarios. This first Professional Experience course will provide the health assessment framework on which clinical assessment will be based.
learning_outcomes: Apply principles of quality and safety including infection prevention and control, quality use of medicines and caring in all aspects of nursing care practice
Demonstrate evidence-based, comprehensive assessment and planning of care that is person-centred, in accordance with relevant policies and clinical practice guidelines
Apply the clinical reasoning to the assessment, planning and implementation of care for individuals and/or groups
Undertake critical reflective practice activities, including receiving and providing constructive feedback, that promotes the development of life-long learning and self-care strategies
Demonstrate an ability to communicate and engage effectively with individuals and teams during simulated learning experiences
Perform and document a range of nursing skills in the simulation environment applying evidence from a range of sources

assessment_tasks.task_name: Students must demonstrate competency in all below listed assessments

title: Professional Experience 2
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course provides opportunities for students to consolidate theoretical knowledge, acquire skills and apply principles of care through case studies informed by the National Health Priority Areas. Within the simulated learning environment (SLE), skill acquisition and rehearsal take place using clinical reasoning with application to authentic simulated patient scenarios. Students will further consolidate the integration of theoretical knowledge and skills during a professional experience placement of 80 hours. The primary focus of this Professional Experience is caring for older people across a range of health care settings and conducting health assessments.
learning_outcomes: Recognise how clinical reasoning informs the assessment, planning and implementation of care for individuals and/or groups.
Demonstrate an ability to communicate and engage effectively with individuals and teams during simulated learning and professional experiences.
Undertake critical reflective practice activities, including receiving and providing constructive feedback, that promotes the development of life-long learning and self-care strategies.
Perform and document a range of nursing skills in the simulation and/or clinical environment applying evidence from a range of sources.
Demonstrate evidence-based, comprehensive assessment and planning of care that is person-centred, in accordance with relevant policies and clinical practice guidelines.
Apply principles of quality and safety, quality use of medicines and caring in all aspects of nursing care.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Students must demonstrate competency in all below listed assessments

title: Foundations of Professional Practice 1A
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course prepares nursing and midwifery students for their roles as knowledgeable and skilled health care professionals. It provides an introduction to and foundation for professional conduct, critical thinking and safe, evidence-based clinical practice
learning_outcomes: Reflect on culture, values, ethics, attitudes, beliefs, assumptions and your own learning
Identify the legal and professional requirements of the Codes of Conduct and Ethics for nurses/midwives in Australia and critically evaluate relevant cases
Explain the nature and implications of patient/woman safety, including causes of adverse events and strategies to reduce their incidence and improve safety
Demonstrate a beginning understanding of types of research and evidence-based practice
Perform effective searches to locate and utilise relevant, high quality evidence-based literature for academic writing
Demonstrate a beginning understanding of the Australian health care system
Discuss law and ethics related to privacy and confidentiality and critically evaluate relevant cases
Examine examples of social, environmental, biomedical and economic determinants of health from a local, national and global perspective
Demonstrate a beginning understanding of person/woman centred care, dignity care, professional boundaries and therapeutic communication
Discuss health literacy, health promotion and models of health behaviour change
Demonstrate a beginning understanding of critical thinking and clinical reasoning, including types of clinical reasoning errors and implications for patient/woman safety
Discuss cultural awareness, competence and safety, including the provision of culturally safe care in a range of health care contexts/situations
Demonstrate understanding of academic literacies requirements

title: Preparation for Clinical Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course prepares students for clinical placements and provides an introduction to clinical practice issues such as self-care, patient safety and professional communication. Mindfulness, mental health first aid, workplace health and safety, safe patient moving, infection control, patient assessment and hygiene, therapeutic and person-centred communication will each be addressed.
learning_outcomes: Identify the differences in scope of practice, accountability and responsibility between students, registered nurses, enrolled nurses and unlicensed health care workers
Demonstrate therapeutic communication skills
Demonstrate a beginning understanding of how to provide support to adults who are developing a mental illness or experiencing a mental health crisis.
Discuss person-centred assessment and apply to the collection of health data/cues
Demonstrate an understanding of your role in maintaining patient safety

Discuss how the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia's competency standards, codes of ethics and codes of professional conduct provide a framework for professional practice and performance assessment
Demonstrate an understanding of relevant aspects of the Workplace Health & Safety Act (2011)
Explain infection control principles and procedures and demonstrate effective hand hygiene
Demonstrate a beginning understanding of the mind-body-spirit connection in health

Identify the importance of mandatory notification requirements in national law in relation to impaired students and reflect on personal factors related to health and well-being that may impact on being fit for practice
Demonstrate ergonomic principles to prevent manual handling injuries and promote patient comfort and safety
Utilise mindfulness strategies to manage person stressors
Demonstrate the ability to reflect on your practice
Undertake the process for NSW Health Verification Requirements for preparation to attend placement
Demonstrate critical thinking and clinical reasoning and their application to health care

assessment_tasks.task_name: Laboratory attendance, assessment of competence and evidence of compulsory requirements

title: Foundations of Professional Practice 1B
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course provides the theoretical foundations to the nursing care of adults and children across a range of clinical contexts. Scenarios based on infection, inflammation, degeneration and injury will provide a platform for the development of critical thinking and clinical reasoning related to assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation and evaluation of nursing care; as well as quality use of medicines. Evidence-based practice and relevant legal and ethical principles are integral to this course.
learning_outcomes: Describe legal requirements related to written and electronic forms of documentation
Identify the significance and impact of evidence-based practice in nursing
Define common terms relating to selected infective, inflammatory, degenerative and injurious conditions
Describe the relationships between the pathophysiology and symptomatology relating to selected infective, inflammatory, degenerative and injurious conditions

Utilise critical thinking skills and clinical reasoning skills in the identification of potential health problems, planning, implementation and evaluation of planning basic nursing care relating to selected infective, inflammatory, degenerative and injurious conditions
Define common terms relating to selected pharmacological and medication-related practice including quality use of medicines

Examine the relevant aspects of common law and legislation relating to professional accountability including: consent and assault; NSW Poisons And Therapeutic Goods Act (1969) and regulation (2008); NSW Ministry of Health policy directive 2007_077 `medication management in NSW public hospitals'; NSW guardianship act (1987) and apply them to specific clinical situations
Identify health care goals that are achievable and congruent with the values, beliefs and cultural practices of individuals/groups
Identify the psychosocial impact of illness and injury on the person and their family
Identify strategies for addressing stigma and marginalization in clinical practice.
Demonstrate an understanding of the demographic and epidemiological trends in ageing.
Use a structured evidence-based assessment framework in collecting data about the physical, socio- cultural and mental health of individuals with health breakdown
Discuss the relationship between person-centred care, therapeutic communication and patient safety
Describe the process for reporting incidents of unsafe or unprofessional medication-related practice to prevent reoccurrence
Discuss elements of professionalism in nursing practice
Describe the areas of practice of other health care professions, opportunities to enhance care through involvement and interprofessional communication and discuss the relationship to patient safety

assessment_tasks.task_name: Closed Book Examination - Accredited Program - use of Memory Aids are not permitted.

title: Clinical Practice 1B
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course provides the clinical foundations to the care of adults and children across a range of contexts. The development of critical thinking and clinical reasoning skills related to assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of nursing care, safe medication practices, relevant legal and ethical principles are integral to this course.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate safe and effective nursing practice consistent with client needs and plan of care including the involvement of other health care professionals
Utilise clinical reasoning skills (cycle) in both simulated settings and clinical practice.
Demonstrate beginning understanding of health informatics and health technology as essential for safe and effective delivery of care
Demonstrate critical thinking skills in the assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of nursing actions
Demonstrate a range of techniques, including observation, interview, physical assessment to conduct a comprehensive nursing assessment
Demonstrate person-centred care in practice
Reflect on nursing practice and identify professional development needs
Demonstrate interprofessional communication skills including the use of ISBAR, patient handover and report writing
Apply professional and ethical nursing frameworks to practice

Students that complete this course will also be able to demonstrate competence in the following core skills at a beginning level: a. taking, assessing and recording the vital signs (including pulse oximetry) b. mobility assessment c. provision of hygiene care d. safe moving of client unable to assist or get out of bed e. Simple dressing technique f. calculation of medication dosages g. medication administration (oral)

Integrate into practice common law and legislation relating to professional practice and accountability including: consent; NSW Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Act (1969) and Regulation (2008); NSW Ministry of Health Policy policies related to: `Medication management in NSW public hospitals; `Health Care Records - Documentation and Management; `Records - Principles for Creation, Management, Storage and Disposal of Health Care Records; and Medical Records
Apply an evidence-based assessment framework to collect data about the physical, socio-cultural and mental health of individuals
Demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between person-centred care, therapeutic communication and patient safety

assessment_tasks.task_name: Clinical Performance (Laboratory, Core Skills and Clinical Summary Sheets)

title: Essentials of Surgical Nursing
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course will provide students with knowledge and principles of perioperative care, to achieve best patient outcomes across the lifespan. The course content comprises the concepts in surgery, infection prevention, preoperative preparation, intraoperative care, wound, and pain management, homeostasis, postoperative complication prevention, and enhanced recovery. The case studies are informed by the National Health Priority Areas. By the end of the course, the students will be able to provide safe and appropriate perioperative care.
learning_outcomes: Identify the legal and ethical principles related to the surgical experience.
Discuss the principles of cultural competence, therapeutic and inter professional communication skills in the plan of care for individuals experiencing surgery.
Demonstrate knowledge of epidemiology, pathophysiology and symptomatology to assist in management of patients' surgical experience.
Relate the Quality Use of Medicines framework to the essentials of surgical nursing care.
Apply the Roper Logan Tierney Model of Nursing and the Clinical Reasoning Cycle across the lifespan to create a plan of care for individuals experiencing surgery.

title: Professional Experience 3
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course provides opportunities for students to consolidate theoretical knowledge, acquire skills and apply principles of care through case studies informed by the National Health Priority Areas. Within the simulated learning environment (SLE), skill acquisition and rehearsal take place using clinical reasoning with application to authentic simulated patient scenarios. Students will further consolidate the integration of theoretical knowledge and skills during a professional experience placement of 160 hours.
learning_outcomes: Apply clinical reasoning to the assessment, planning and implementation of care for individuals and/or groups experiencing surgery.
Practice principles of quality and safety, quality use of medicines and caring in all aspects of nursing care.
Demonstrate an ability to communicate and engage effectively with individuals and teams during simulated and professional learning experiences.
Undertake critical reflective practice activities, including receiving and providing constructive feedback, that promotes the development of life-long learning and self-care strategies.
Perform and document a range of nursing skills in the simulation and/or clinical environment applying evidence from a range of sources.
Demonstrate evidence-based, comprehensive assessment and planning of care that is person-centred, in accordance with relevant policies and clinical practice guidelines.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Students must demonstrate competency in all below listed assessments

title: Essentials of Medical Nursing
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course provides students with knowledge and principles of the management of care of adults and children with specified medical situations across a range of clinical contexts. The case studies are informed by the National Health Priority Areas. By the end of the course students will be able to plan safe and appropriate care and recognize the impact of these diseases on individuals, family, and communities at acute, chronic and rehabilitation contexts.
learning_outcomes: Relate the Quality Use of Medicines framework to the essentials of medical nursing care.
Discuss the principles of cultural competence, therapeutic and inter professional communication skills when planning care for people experiencing medical conditions.
Apply the Roper Logan Tierney Model of Nursing and the Clinical Reasoning Cycle across the lifespan to create a plan of care for individuals experiencing medical conditions.
Identify the legal and ethical principles related to nursing medical conditions.
Demonstrate knowledge of epidemiology, pathophysiology and symptomatology to assist in management of nursing medical conditions.

title: Professional Experience 4
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course provides opportunities for students to consolidate theoretical knowledge, acquire skills and apply principles of care through case studies informed by the National Health Priority Areas. Within the simulated learning environment (SLE), skill acquisition and rehearsal take place using clinical reasoning with application to authentic simulated patient scenarios. Students will further consolidate the integration of theoretical knowledge and skills during a professional experience placement of 160 hours.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate evidence-based, comprehensive assessment and planning of care that is person-centred, in accordance with relevant policies and clinical practice guidelines.
Demonstrate an ability to communicate and engage effectively with individuals and teams during simulated and professional learning experiences.
Undertake critical reflective practice activities, engage in receiving and providing constructive feedback, that results in the development of life-long learning and self-care strategies.
Practice principles of quality and safety, quality use of medicines and caring in all aspects of nursing care practice.
Apply the clinical reasoning to the assessment, planning and implementation of care for individuals and/or groups.
Perform and document a range of nursing skills in the simulation and/or clinical environment applying evidence from a range of sources.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Students must demonstrate competency in all below listed assessments

title: Essentials of Health Promotion
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course introduces students to concepts and principles of public health and health promotion. Student will use health promotion and primary health care as defined by the World Health Organization and the framework of social determinants of health, students will examine professional roles, cultural safety and public health initiatives. This course introduces students to contemporary public health and health promotion issues including: definitions and components of health; health status indicators and outcomes; epidemiological terms and principles; approaches to health promotion and illness prevention; health behaviour change strategies; health/illness care systems; and current issues in local, national and international health.
learning_outcomes: Identify selected health promotion and practice activities across the lifespan using contemporary models of primary health care to enhance health and wellbeing outcomes.
Understand health promotion, public health and community practice.
Assess a person's health promotion needs acknowledging the influence of values, beliefs, culture and diversity.
Demonstrate how the social determinants of health impact health and wellbeing outcomes of diverse groups.
Explain the principles of population health and epidemiology including the concepts of prevalence and incidence, morbidity and mortality, prevention and treatment and cost.
Explore how health promotion addresses the national health priorities.

title: Clinical Practice 2A
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course provides the clinical foundations to the care of adults and children across a range of contexts. The development of critical thinking and clinical reasoning skills related to assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of nursing care, safe medication practices and relevant ethical and legal principles are integral to this course. This course includes a professional experience placement of 4 weeks duration.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate safe and legal administration of intravenous fluids and medications: including insulin infusion administration and analgesia by IMI and using a PCA in a simulated setting
Demonstrate safe and professional nursing care when managing a stoma and a enteral tube feeding in a simulated setting

Demonstrate a level of competence commensurate with a second year nursing student in the following core skills: a) intravenous therapy (IVT) (establishment & management) b) intramuscular medication administration c) Comprehensive pain assessment d) Mental Health assessment (depending on NURS2103 enrolment)
Demonstrate safe and effective written and verbal communication skills when providing care.

Plan and provide person centred, safe, ethical and legal professional nursing care to patients in a clinical setting (settings include but are not restricted to mental health, ageing, acute, rehabilitation, community, justice) with the involvement of other health professionals
Simulate effective communication when providing palliative and end-of-life person-centred care

Demonstrate appropriate nursing practice in accordance with the Registered Nurse Standards for Practice including the ability to communicate in English with patients and staff in the clinical environment
Apply knowledge and skills in the assessment and management of fluid/electrolyte status and pain in a pre-operative and/or post-operative simulated setting.
Demonstrate safe and professional nursing care when managing acute and chronic wounds in a simulated setting
Demonstrate the ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with consumers, families, carers and the interdisciplinary team in the clinical environment

assessment_tasks.task_name: Clinical Performance (Simulation Learning, Core Skills and ANSAT)

title: Foundations of Professional Practice 2A
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course provides the theoretical foundations to the nursing care of adults and children across a range of clinical contexts. The gastrointestinal, endocrine and kidney diseases that feature in the clinical scenarios selected for this course are based on Australia's National Health Priority Areas and the impact of these diseases on morbidity and mortality. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health; evidence-based practice; relevant legal and ethical principles are integral to this course.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the importance of person centred and family centred care in safe and effective care delivery
Use clinical reasoning to identify nursing problems in the patient scenarios being studied and plan safe effective nursing care and patient education
Utilise nursing research to support best practice nursing actions and critically appraise qualitative research and its application to empathetic patient care.
Identify the importance of effective inter-professional communication to safe practice and the prevention of medication error
Explain and apply legal and ethical concepts including beneficence, non-maleficence, negligence, open disclosure, and mandatory reporting
Demonstrate mastery of required medication and intravenous fluid calculations
Discuss the epidemiology, pathophysiology and symptomatology of the health breakdown of conditions being studied
Identify the attribute and skills required for culturally competent practice and apply to scenarios being studied

assessment_tasks.task_name: Closed Book Examination - Accredited Program - use of Memory Aids are not permitted.

title: Essentials of Mental Health Nursing
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: An introductory knowledge about mental health is essential for all nursing graduates. The establishment and maintenance of an empathic therapeutic person-centred relationship with consumers is central to all aspects of mental health nursing. Concepts covered in this course are informed by evidence and promote the rights of mental health consumers and carers to be fully engaged in their health promotion, assessment, treatment and recovery in collaboration with health professionals who provide mental health care. By the end of the course students will be able to contribute to the facilitation of recovery of mental health consumers by focusing on incorporating strengths and wellbeing in mental health care delivery in the nursing context.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate relevant knowledge, skills and attributes in mental health nursing.
Explain how the recovery of mental health consumers is facilitated by focussing on their strengths and wellbeing.
Identify the rights of mental health consumers, carers and significant others to lead their treatment and the recovery process.
Identify strategies to develop empathic, compassionate and professional therapeutic relationships with mental health consumers, carers, and significant others.
Discuss the rights of mental health consumers to live free from discrimination and social exclusion.
Plan, develop, and evaluate evidence-based initiatives that promote mental health, prevent and intervene early in illness, facilitate recovery and promote wellbeing.

title: Essentials of Palliative Care
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course will enable students to develop principles of person centred, evidence-based nursing care for people with a life limiting illness across the lifespan and apply the principle of palliative care. The case studies are informed by the National Health Priority Areas. There will be a strong focus on promoting dignity and quality of life for the palliative care person and their family. By the end of the course the student will be able to apply evidenced based practice across a variety of settings using a clinical reasoning approach.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on their own personal values and beliefs about dying and death and the lived experience of the dying person, their families and communities.
Demonstrate advanced pathophysiology knowledge to manage common symptoms in the palliative care environment.
Identify the legal and ethical principles related to caring for people with a life limiting illness.
Critically evaluate the efficacy of pharmacological and nonpharmacological (complementary therapies) in the palliative care context.
Demonstrate advanced understanding of developmental, lifespan, social spiritual and cultural factors that impact on the quality of life for people with a life limiting illness.
Apply the Clinical Reasoning Cycle across the lifespan to create a plan of care for individuals experiencing a life limiting illness across contexts of nursing practice.

title: Clinical Practice 2B
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course provides the clinical foundations to the care of adults and children across a range of contexts. The development of critical thinking and clinical reasoning skills related to assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of nursing care, safe medication practices, relevant legal and ethical principles are integral to this course. The course includes 4 weeks clinical placement.
learning_outcomes: Assessment and management of the deteriorating patient with respect to myocardial infarction in a simulated environment
Therapeutic communication with a person who has cognitive and/or sensory impairment to ensure patient safety
Demonstrate the ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with consumers, families, carers and the interdisciplinary team in the clinical environment

Students that complete this course will also be able to demonstrate competence in the following core skills at a second year level: a) oxygen administration b) intravenous medication administration via bolus and burette

Demonstrate appropriate nursing practice in accordance with the Registered Nurse Standards for Practice including the ability to communicate in English with patients and staff in the clinical environment
Engage in reflection of nursing care of people with cardiovascular, respiratory and neurological chronic and acute conditions to identify professional development needs in a simulated setting
Demonstrate safe and professional nursing care in the provision of care for a person who has had a stroke, cardiac or respiratory event using the clinical reasoning cycle in a simulated environment

Plan and provide person centred safe, ethical and legal professional nursing care to at least 2 patient in a clinical setting (settings include but are not restricted to mental health, ageing, acute, rehabilitation, community, justice health) with the involvement of other health professionals
Assessment and management of cardiovascular, respiratory and neurological chronic and acute conditions in a simulated environment
Demonstrate the provision of person-centred and culturally competent care to people with cardiovascular, respiratory and neurological in a simulated environment

assessment_tasks.task_name: Clinical Performance (Laboratory, Core Skills and Clinical attendance and performance)

Within the simulated learning environment (SLE), skill acquisition and rehearsal take place using clinical reasoning with application to authentic simulated patient scenarios. Students will further consolidate the integration of theoretical knowledge and skills during a professional experience placement of 160 hours.
learning_outcomes: Apply clinical reasoning to the assessment, planning and implementation of care for individuals and/or groups.
Incorporate reflective practice activities in daily practice, including receiving and providing constructive feedback, that result in the development of life-long learning and self-care strategies.

Demonstrate evidence-based, comprehensive assessment and planning of care that is person-centred, in accordance with relevant policies and clinical practice guidelines.
Demonstrate an ability to communicate and engage effectively with individuals and teams during simulated learning and professional experiences.

title: Essentials of Nursing the Deteriorating Person
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course provides students with knowledge and principles of care for the deteriorating person. Students apply systematic health assessment frameworks and evidence-based practice to describe safe, effective and culturally appropriate care across the lifespan. Students will develop skills to recognise and analyse deteriorating patient situations, related to National Health Priority areas. A variety of case-studies will enable students to plan, implement and evaluate time critical care actions. By the end of this course students will understand the principles of acute care nursing across a variety of critical care contexts.
learning_outcomes: Integrate and relate legal and ethical principles in the planning of care for the deteriorating person.
Discuss the principles of cultural competence, therapeutic and inter professional communication skills when planning care for deteriorating people.

Implement clinical reasoning, comprehensive patient assessment to recognise, respond, communicate and advocate in time-critical situations involving the deteriorating person, as part of the multidisciplinary team approach.
Evaluate and reflect on knowledge for coping with experiencing grief, loss and bereavement concerning the deteriorating person, families and staff.
Apply the Quality Use of Medicines Framework to the care of deteriorating patients in a range of contexts.
Demonstrate knowledge of pathophysiology, risk factors, multi morbidities and epidemiology of select diseases linked to the rapidly deteriorating person across the lifespan.

title: Essentials of Chronic Illness and Disability
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course provides students with an understanding of the impact chronic illness and disability have on the health of people, their family, and the community. On completion of this course, students will develop foundational knowledge through case study engagement, informed by the National Health Priority Areas, to apply evidence-based, safe, holistic, culturally appropriate and person-centred care to people with chronic illness and disability across the lifespan.
learning_outcomes: Apply an advanced understanding of pathophysiology to select chronic illnesses and/or disabilities.
Identify priority populations for the prevention and management of chronic illness and/or disability.
Plan safe, effective, evidence-based, and culturally sensitive care to optimise the quality of life of people with chronic illness and/or disability across a range of contexts.
Explain the role of the nurse in the multidisciplinary team in the prevention and management of chronic illness and/or disability.
Apply legal and ethical principles to the care of people with chronic illness and/or disability and their families.
Identify the impact of physical, psychosocial, cultural, spiritual and financial factors on the lives of people with chronic illness and/or disability in Australia.

title: Transition to Professional Nursing
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course explores contemporary issues associated with the transition from student to registered nurse within a variety of health care settings. This course will build students' knowledge and strategies in areas of teamwork, clinical decision making, critical thinking, advocacy, organisation culture and responding to changes in health care environments in relation to technology and models of care delivery. This will consolidate the concepts delivered in theoretical and practice courses to facilitate the transition into the role of a registered nurse.
learning_outcomes: Identify the role of evidence-based practice and learning opportunities play in the transformation of their practice as a registered nurse.
Analyse information sources including health and nursing informatics in the management of health environments.
Critically discuss the challenges, factors and strategies in the transition from student to registered nurse.
Critique the professional roles and responsibilities of being a registered nurse in the Australian health-care environment.
Appraise the strategies to promote resilience and build capacity in the transition from student to registered nurse.

title: Professional Experience 6
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The capstone course provides opportunities for students to consolidate theoretical knowledge and skills and apply principles of care through case studies informed by the National Health Priority Areas. Within the simulated learning environment (SLE), skill acquisition and rehearsal take place using clinical reasoning with application to authentic simulated patient scenarios. Students will further consolidate the integration of theoretical knowledge and skills during a professional experience placement of 240 hours.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate evidence-based, comprehensive and complex assessment and planning of care that is person-centred, in accordance with relevant policies and clinical practice guidelines.
Demonstrate an ability to communicate and engage effectively with individuals and teams during simulated and professional learning experiences.
Incorporate critical reflective activities in daily practice, including receiving and providing constructive feedback, that promotes the development of life-long learning and self-care strategies.
Perform and document a range of nursing skills in the simulation and/or clinical environment applying evidence from a range of sources.
Evaluate the application of clinical reasoning to the assessment, planning and implementation of care for individuals and/or groups with complex and /or deteriorating care needs.
Practice and appraise principles of quality and safety, quality use of medicines and caring in all aspects of nursing care practice.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Students must demonstrate competency in all below listed assessments

title: Healthy Ageing Across Contexts and Communities
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course will enhance students' understanding of person-centred care, healthy ageing and the management of acute and chronic conditions experienced by older people. Factors that impact on health and the delivery of primary, secondary and tertiary health care for older people in Australia are discussed. An older person interprofessional framework, which promotes wellness across a range of contexts, will be introduced. The neuropathology of mild cognitive impairment, dementia, delirium and depression will also be addressed. Clinical scenarios will be used to explore innovative management related to nursing older people. In these scenarios relevant ethico-legal, socio-political, cultural, and spiritual issues are also covered
learning_outcomes: Utilise critical thinking and clinical reasoning skills in the management of older people experiencing delirium, dementia, depression and acute illness superimposed on chronic conditions
Utilise an evidence-based assessment framework to collect information about the physical, socio-cultural, psychological, cultural and spiritual needs of older people
Apply relevant health promotion strategies to older people and their family/carers related to normal ageing processes and chronic and complex health conditions (including self-management)
Identify ethico-legal, cultural and spiritual issues related to end-of-life care/palliative care, across care contexts
Discuss the importance of working with older people and their carers to develop a healthy ageing plan of care
Recognise the predisposing and precipitating factors for and pathophysiology of mild cognitive impairment, dementia, delirium, depression
Identify strategies to maximise continuity of care and healthy ageing for older people when transitioning across care contexts
Discuss the concepts of person-centred care, healthy ageing and optimising the health of older people and their family/carers

title: Clinical Practice 3A
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course provides the clinical foundations to the nursing management of patients across the age continuum. The demonstration of critical thinking and clinical reasoning skills related to assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of nursing care and effective communication and teamwork are integral to this course. The course includes a professional experience placement of 5 weeks duration
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate appropriate nursing practice in accordance with the Registered Nurse Standards for Practice (2016) including the ability to communicate in English with patients and staff in the clinical environment
Demonstrate the ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with consumers, families, carers and the interprofessional team in the clinical environment
