Plan and provide evidence based, person centred, culturally competent, safe, ethical and legal professional nursing care to patients in a clinical setting with the involvement of other health professionals
Demonstrate safe and effective written and verbal communication skills when providing care.
Demonstrate knowledge and application of safe and legal administration of intravenous fluids and medications: including IVI analgesia in a simulated environment
Apply knowledge and skills in the assessment and management of critically ill patient's airway and breathing, including tracheostomy care in a simulated environment.
Demonstrate knowledge and application of safe and professional nursing care when managing urinary catheterisation (female) in a simulated environment
Apply knowledge and skills of effective communication, teamwork and timely patient assessment and escalation for optimal patient outcomes in a simulated environment
Apply knowledge and skills in the primary and secondary assessment and management of critically ill patient with a trauma injury in a simulated setting.
Demonstrate knowledge and application of safe and professional nursing care when managing central line care, blood transfusions and underwater seal drains in a simulated clinical environment
Critically reflect on clinical placement experience and performance and identify strategies to improve future professional practice

assessment_tasks.task_name: Students must demonstrate competency in all below listed assessments
Clinical Placement Performance (Simulation Learning, Core Skills and ANSAT)

title: Supervised Project
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course will enable students to undertake a project related to health, nursing, or midwifery under the close supervision of an academic staff member.
learning_outcomes: Discuss health within a selected health context using one or more of the following: relevant professional standards, concepts of health, models of health care, determinants of health or health promotion/health breakdown prevention.
Demonstrate advanced critical evaluation, synthesis, and application of evidence to support written and verbal discussions
Demonstrate effective verbal and written communication, in a way that is sensitive to cultural diversity

title: Foundations of Professional Practice 3A
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course focuses on the assessment and prioritisation of care in the management of injury in adults and children. Evidence-based research is used to explore topics including road accidents, burns, blast, drowning, sepsis, shock, traumatic brain injury, spinal injury, fracture, and disaster management. It Includes principles and practices of triage, massive blood transfusion, and cultural competency in critical care. The legal principles and ethical concepts relating to end of life care are integral to this course.
learning_outcomes: Recognise the increased risk of post - traumatic stress disorder for people experiencing catastrophic physical events, their carers, and identify effective strategies for responding to such stressors
Explain the management of Acute Behavioural Disturbance and how inter-professional communication enables patient advocacy
Demonstrate effective verbal and written communication in peer education related to selected clinical situations
Demonstrate knowledge of pathophysiology, epidemiology, mechanism of injury and quality use of medicines principles relating to selected critical care scenarios.
Apply clinical reasoning skills and evidence based practice to develop plans of nursing care in selected critical care scenarios
Identify how person-centred-care principles, cultural competence and therapeutic relationships are used to support individuals at end-of-life or who are experiencing grief, loss and bereavement
Demonstrate competency in required medication and intravenous fluid calculations

title: Leading, Teaching, Mentoring and Clinical Supervision for Health Professionals
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course is premised on the belief that effective leadership, mentoring and clinical teaching can transform practice. It examines theories relevant to adult learning, leadership, mentorship, preceptorship, and clinical supervision. Students will be provided with opportunities to integrate this knowledge into their own clinical practice and to reflect on and learn from this experience.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge, skills and understanding integral to adult learning principles and teaching practices
Demonstrate knowledge, skills and understanding integral to leadership in the contemporary health care environment
Demonstrate knowledge, skills and understanding integral to mentorship, preceptorship and clinical supervision

title: Health Research Methods
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The main component of the Honours program is an original research project on a topic relevant to nursing/midwifery practice, conducted under the close supervision of an academic staff member. In this course the student will need to work with their supervisor/s to develop a research question and then develop the proposal for their project. The student will acquire the skills of developing a research proposal and an ethics application. They will be required to explore and develop skills in the application of research methods relevant to the research project they are undertaking. They will be required to identify a research problem, select an appropriate research technique and describe the associated ethical considerations. The student will be required to present a seminar on their identified research design and method
learning_outcomes: identify and describe the ethical implications of undertaking research with humans
present clear and coherent verbal and written communication of a research problem, design and method
select appropriate research techniques;
identify research problems;

title: Transition to Professional Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This is the capstone course for Bachelor of Nursing. The course requires students to integrate and apply the knowledge, concepts and skills associated with their entire sequence of undergraduate study. Students have an extended clinical placement in one of a range of contexts in which they are required to demonstrate their ability to practice at the level of a competent beginning registered nurse. Transition to the role of registered nurse, clinical competence and safety and quality in health care are the primary focus of this course. This course includes 5 weeks clinical placement
learning_outcomes: Identify and use appropriate personal strategies and support networks to manage the stress inherent in professional practice;
Demonstrate capability to practice according to the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia Registered Nurse Standards for Practice;
Describe the importance of quality improvement, clinical audits and risk management activities;
Demonstrate effective clinical reasoning skills and analyses nursing practice;
Reflect on and learn from clinical practice experiences;
Engage in therapeutic and professional communication and contribute effectively as a member of the interdisciplinary health care team.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Students must demonstrate competency in all below listed assessments

title: Reviewing and Critiquing Literature
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The main component of the Honours program is an original research project on a topic relevant to nursing/midwifery practice, conducted under the close supervision of an academic staff member. In this course the student will be required to develop and justify search strategies and undertake a search of the academic and professional literature relevant to the research project they are undertaking. They will be required to read, understand and critically evaluate literature
learning_outcomes: Synthesis and presentation of a comprehensive literature review to guide a research thesis.
Implement a literature search with data extraction & critique of included studies
Develop a search & extraction strategy that includes search terms, & data bases
Formulate an operational research question which enables the framing of the literature research

title: Research Progress
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The main component of the Honours program is an original research project conducted under the close supervision of an academic staff member. In this course it is anticipated that students will work with supervisors on a project that has attained ethics approval if relevant. Students will undertake data collection, management, analysis and interpretation related to their project in collaboration with project supervisor/s.
learning_outcomes: demonstrate capacity for effective data collection, data management , analysis and interpretation
communicate project progress through the completion of a research progress report and seminar.

title: Youth and Young Adult Mental Health: 12 to 24 Years
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course provides health care practitioners with the theoretical knowledge and clinical skills development to appropriately and effectively assess and work with youth and young adults in mental health and non-mental health settings. The course develops theory and skills to recognise, intervene and prevent mental health problems in the older age group. The course will cover aspects of care related to risk management, assessment, parent/carer education, specific clinical practice skills and hand-over-of-care/integrated care planning for mental health inpatient, adolescent, young adult and other hospital settings, Justice Health and other paediatric settings, child and family health and out-of-home settings. Assessment tasks are focused on Youth and Young Adult Mental Health (12 years to 24 years of age) therefore, you will need to have access to this group. There is some flexibility in this, but you need to contact the Course Coordinator. The course includes content relevant to rural and remote settings and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander youth and young adult mental health care within government and non-government clinical services.
learning_outcomes: Examine the mental health disparities in relation to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander and Non-Indigenous youth and young adults in Australia and how appropriate mental health care strategies can help close the gap.
Demonstrate effective communication with patients and their families and within a multi or interdisciplinary or inter-agency mental health care team.

Develop a plan of care for youth and young adult (12-24 yrs.) with a mental health disturbance or illness, which demonstrates the provision of holistic care including the family/carer using current evidence and theories.
Reflect on current practice and plan ongoing development commensurate with personal and professional goals
Undertake appropriate mental health assessment and risk management with sound clinical judgment compliant with best practice and policy guidelines for youth and young adult (12-24 yrs.)
Retrieve, critique and apply evidenced based literature to inform clinical practice decisions when working with young people experiencing mental disturbance or illness.

title: Health and Substance Misuse
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Prepares students to assess and manage people with substance misuse problems particularly those with a co-morbidity of mental illness. The course uses comprehensive assessment and brief interventions and appropriate therapies. Domains of learning include pharmacotherapy, prevention strategies, the pathophysiology of substance misuse and a sociological perspective on substance misuse.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and provide appropriate psychotherapies
Describe and deliver appropriate brief interventions
Conduct a comprehensive Alcohol and Other Drugs assessment
Advise on harm-minimisation and prevention strategies
Critically evaluate current pharmacotherapies used in the treatment of substance misuse
Assess readiness for change based on Stages of Change model
Examine and criticise the multi-factorial determinants for substance misuse

title: Therapeutic Engagement and Psychosocial Interventions
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course is designed to support the further development of the student's ability and skills to engage therapeutically. The course provides an overview of psychosocial interventions and the history of the development and use of talking therapies. Students will gain a working knowledge of a broad range of psychosocial and psycho-educational interventions, including the emerging area of e-therapy. The course will assist students to ensure consumers receive the most appropriate therapeutic options and encourage the development of further knowledge and skills in an intervention of their own choosing. Students will be encouraged to consider the challenges arising when working in multicultural and Indigenous Australian settings.
learning_outcomes: Appraise a range of therapeutic options for a particular client and critique the research evidence supporting your recommendations for the choice of intervention

Utilise reflective practice principles to identify personal values, ethical issues and practice issues arising in mental health clinical practice and to discuss the changes you have made to your practice as an outcome of completing this course.
Critique the application of western-developed interventions with reference to cultural safety in Indigenous Australian and multicultural settings
Describe the impact of growing understandings of neurophysiology of psychotherapy and the role of therapeutic engagement in enhancing the effectiveness of psychosocial interventions
Analyse and critique the theoretical foundations, techniques and value of a range of psychosocial interventions, including individual, group based and e-therapies
Demonstrate a sound knowledge of one psychotherapeutic intervention of your own choosing and identify your proposal to increase your skills in delivering this intervention.

title: Honours Thesis Completion
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The main component of the Honours program is an original research project conducted under the close supervision of an academic staff member. In this course the student will need to work under the guidance of their supervisor/s to finalise their project with a clear and coherent written report. This report will demonstrate a sound understanding of the research process and the ability to report the outcomes of the project in a scholarly manner
learning_outcomes: Have submitted a clear and coherent written report in the form of a thesis dissertation or journal manuscript

title: Acute Nursing Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The advance practice nurse requires diverse knowledge to appropriately and effectively assess and manage patients in an acute care environment. This course builds on the knowledge and leadership of nurses in these settings and includes development of expert, specialised cognitive and technical skills to prepare nurses for advance practice roles in acute care nursing. By the end of the course students will have developed advanced practice knowledge to enhance the quality and safety of care for people with an acute illness and enhance their ability to influence care outcomes for both individuals and groups of patients within their chosen acute care setting.
learning_outcomes: Examine the role of clinical leadership in acute nursing practice and identify personal strategies to enhance your own leadership skills
Critically evaluate professional nursing practice issues that support high quality nursing care for people with an acute illness

integrate and critically apply knowledge of clinical governance systems (including the National Safety and Quality Health Service [NSQHS] Standards and risk management principles), and legal and ethical frameworks to provide safe, efficient, effective and culturally appropriate care to acutely unwell individuals
appraise knowledge of acute evidence-based nursing care and integrate into practice to ensure clinical excellence across contexts of acute specialist areas

title: Digital Mental Health Nursing
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course delves into the dynamic intersection of digital mental health nursing, developing technologies, and ethical considerations. Focused on the integration of digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, virtual and augmented reality, ethics, trust, communication of data, and wearable technology, participants will embark on a comprehensive exploration of the evolving landscape in mental health care. It empowers participants to navigate the landscape of digital mental health nursing, equipping them with the knowledge and skills needed to provide inclusive, ethical, and culturally competent care within diverse mental health settings.
learning_outcomes: Explore the fundamental principles of digital mental health nursing to diverse audiences, elucidating the intricate intersection of technology and mental health care.
Explore the ethical implications and challenges associated with integrating technology into mental health practices.

Apply change management principles in the context of digital mental health nursing, demonstrating the ability to strategically plan, implement, and oversee the adoption of digital health technologies within mental health care settings.

Recognise the significance of cultural competence in delivering inclusive digital mental health care to Indigenous and Cultural and Linguistically Diverse peoples in the context of mental health practice.
Critically evaluate case studies to understand and address ethical dilemmas that may arise in digital mental health nursing, developing a nuanced approach to ethical decision-making.

Critically evaluate the role of artificial intelligence and machine learning in shaping mental health interventions, investigating the application of virtual and augmented reality, and recognizing the potential of wearable technology in monitoring and improving mental health outcomes.

Explore and develop strategies to establish and maintain trust between healthcare providers, technology, and patients, while also acquiring skills in effectively communicating data generated by digital tools.

title: Emergency Nursing Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The emergency nurse requires diverse knowledge to appropriately and effectively assess and manage patients in the emergency department. This course builds on the skills, knowledge and leadership of nurses in emergency department settings and includes development of expert, specialised cognitive and technical skills to prepare nurses for advance practice roles in the emergency department environment. By the end of the course students will have developed advanced practice skills to enhance the quality and safety of care for people within the emergency department and enhance their ability to influence care outcomes for these individuals and groups of patients, as well as their families.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of healthcare systems, emergency department settings and the role of the registered nurse to provide safe, efficient, effective and culturally appropriate care of people in emergency departments
Critically evaluate emergency department models of care and demonstrate their application across contexts of care in emergency departments
Evaluate and integrate knowledge from nursing science and evidence-based practice to comprehensively assess and manage people in emergency department settings
Plan future improvement within an emergency department context through the evaluation and development of a practice improvement program
Evaluate theories of clinical leadership and identify strategies to develop your leadership within interdisciplinary teams in the emergency department context

title: Mental Health Acute Care
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with an opportunity to advance their knowledge and skills in mental health nursing. The course includes comprehensive assessment, identifying risk factors, safety planning, formulation, diagnostic impressions and collaborative care planning in the acute mental health setting. Students will be encouraged to explore a collaborative, recovery based and trauma informed approach to practice that recognises contributing factors including the role of the consumer, cultural sensitivities, and co-morbid physical health problems on mental health and wellbeing.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the role of clinical formulation and diagnostic impressions within mental health assessments, including the impact of comorbid physical health issues, and evaluate their contribution to treatment planning and evidence-based management strategies.

Critically evaluate the impact of restrictive practices, ethical dilemmas, and cultural safety issues within acute mental health care, and analyse models aimed at reducing restrictive practices and supporting vulnerable populations.

Explore how trauma affects individuals experiencing acute mental health crises, and apply trauma-informed, recovery-oriented care that addresses their foundational needs for safety, belonging, and esteem, while recognising their lived experiences.
Demonstrate an advanced understanding of a consumer-focused comprehensive mental health assessment within the acute mental health settings that is trauma-informed and recovery-oriented.
Assess current psychopharmacological interventions and explain the role of mental health nurses in supporting safe medication use for consumers within acute mental health settings.
Demonstrate skills in developing collaborative care plans with consumers that are trauma-informed and recovery-oriented, including carer involvement.

title: Contemporary Mental Health
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course provides core foundational studies in the Master of Mental Health Nursing program, focusing on developing an understanding of the theoretical basis to and history of mental health nursing; the role of mental health nurses in contemporary mental health care; the impact on the discipline of emerging models of service delivery and the emergence of clinical supervision as a strategy for the development of mental health nursing practice.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate cultural competence by incorporating cultural beliefs and cultural safety into aspects of practice through exploring ways in which effective cross-cultural mental health nursing can be developed;
Compare and contrast the roles, characteristics and impact of advanced mental health nursing practice in the context of global, national and local mental health policy directions;
Critically evaluate the role of clinical supervision as a governance strategy within a framework of safe advanced mental health nursing care.
Demonstrate advanced knowledge of integrated clinical governance strategies and their relationship to advanced practice in mental health nursing;

Synthesise their understanding of historical, socio-cultural, political, legal and professional factors, and health system structures and reforms that influence clinical practice, education and safety in mental health service provision;
Demonstrate a capacity to identify and influence discussion on a range of contemporary issues in mental health nursing;

title: Lived Experience Perspectives in Mental Health Nursing
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course will allow nurses to extend their clinical practice by exploring lived experience perspectives on the important elements of care and mental health service provision. The course will challenge students to critically analyse current healthcare systems and practices and reflect on alternative approaches to mental healthcare provision. The course has a focus on current and future mental healthcare in the context of human rights, history, and peer support and leadership.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the history of psychiatric and nursing practices, how that gave rise to the survivor movement, and reflect on subsequent changes in service provision and how it relates to current and future practices.

Demonstrate an understanding of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) and the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), critically analyse the relationship between these frameworks and mental health service provision, and reflect on the nurse’s role in upholding human rights.
Critically analyse and challenge practice in the context of hope- and recovery-based healthcare for people with mental ill health and distress.
Incorporate an understanding of the socio-political contexts for people’s ill health and distress into their mental health nursing practice.
Demonstrate an understanding of the importance of peer support workers and consumer leaders in mental healthcare, the challenges they face, and of positive ways to collaborate in the workplace.

title: Mental Health of Older People
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Mental Health Nursing offers a valuable contribution to the care of older people. The complex interaction of physical, psychological, cognitive, behavioural and social stressors, resources and strengths can affect the older person's function, health, mental state and quality of life. Fifteen to twenty percent of older people have significant mental health problems. The mental health disorders experienced by the elderly are often overlooked, misdiagnosed or mistreated, leading to high co-morbidity and increasing health care costs, but perhaps most importantly leads to unnecessary suffering and compromised ability to lead life to the fullest. This unique course encompasses knowledge and skills from the disciplines of mental health and aged care nursing, psychiatry, psychology, geriatric medicine and pharmacology. Major diagnostic syndromes, complex clinical assessment and mental health nursing interventions are emphasised as well as an understanding of the psychosocial effects of ageing on mental health.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate related knowledge in the care of the older person who exhibits behavioural symptoms: aggression, disorientation, confusion, paranoia, hallucinations, withdrawal, neglect and disinhibition.
Develop an awareness of theoretical frameworks that explain the notion of successful ageing and apply these theoretical frameworks to your clinical practice
Describe the phenomenology, aetiology, demographics, treatment, and prognosis of psychiatric disorders of old age: mood disorders and psychotic disorders.
Identify the developmental, psychological and psychosocial factors influencing the behaviour of an older person experiencing mental health problems
Recognise the physical and psychological factors affecting the assessment, treatment, care, and management of the older person with mental health problems
Identify common psychiatric or mental health presentations in the older person
Demonstrate skills in comprehensive assessment of the older person within their systems
Explain the potential changing roles of a person as they reach old age and potential associated life problems
Describe the indication, clinical use, effectiveness, adverse effects, potential interactions and nursing implications of the use of common psychoactive medications for the older person
Explain models of nursing intervention based on problem solving, communication, therapies, environment change and somatic treatments
Discuss how co-morbidities, atypical presentations and age-related changes affect diagnosis, treatment and management of the older person with mental health problems

title: Fundamentals of Forensic Mental Health Nursing
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course provides mental health nursing professionals with the fundamental knowledge and skills required to effectively provide therapy and interventions for individuals in forensic settings. Students will learn about the unique challenges and ethical considerations associated with working in forensic mental health settings, and they will develop expertise in evidence-based therapeutic techniques and interventions for improving outcomes. Students will engage in a comprehensive exploration of the critical aspects of nursing in secure forensic settings, with emphasis on the establishment of safe and effective relationships while addressing the unique challenges encountered. This contemporary curriculum was designed by forensic mental health nursing experts. It encompasses a broad range of topics and skills designed to equip mental health nurses with the fundamental knowledge needed to provide safe and effective mental health care in forensic settings.
learning_outcomes: Identify and evaluate the ethical considerations and challenges associated with providing care in forensic settings.
Describe the fundamentals of the nurse-client relationship and relational security in a secure forensic setting.
Define and apply recovery principles specific to the field of forensic nursing, with a focus on transcultural rehabilitation, reintegration, and recidivism as a goal.
Recognise the signs and symptoms of vicarious trauma, burnout, and compassion fatigue in forensic nursing, and employ strategies to mitigate these effects.
Demonstrate knowledge and proficiency in the assessment and management of restrictive practices within a secure forensic environment.
Utilise evidence-based tools and techniques to assess and manage risks effectively within forensic populations.
Analyse the impact of trauma on consumer in forensic settings and apply trauma-informed care principles to improve outcomes.

title: Advanced Forensic Mental Health Nursing
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Forensic mental health nursing is a rewarding and dynamic specialty field that requires specialised education and clinical expertise to address the complex and challenging issues that arise when working with offenders who are experiencing severe and enduring mental illness. Forensic mental health nurses play a crucial role in supporting these consumers on their recovery journey to meet their individualised mental health and criminogenic needs. Our contemporary curriculum is designed by forensic mental health nursing experts. It encompasses a broad range of topics and skills designed to equip mental health nurses with the knowledge and tools needed to provide safe and effective mental health care in forensic settings.
learning_outcomes: Apply ethical and legal standards specific to forensic mental health nursing, assessing their impact on care and safety.
Critically analyse associations between mental health disorders and offending behaviour.
Create and develop effective mental health nursing strategies for collaboration with families in the forensic mental health setting.
Critically appraise the special considerations when delivering mental health nursing care to forensic populations.
Analyse the scope of practice for forensic mental health nursing, differentiating it from other specialties.
Justify mental health nursing interventions that consider unique mental health needs and challenges of diverse populations in the forensic context.

title: Nurse Practitioner Professional Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Registered nurses begin their formal journey towards endorsement as a Nurse Practitioner in Australia with this course. Students will enhance their understandings of the legal, political, social and health factors underpinning the evidence-informed health service provision of advanced clinical practice. A review of major pathology is undertaken so as students may then apply advanced understandings to the culturally, legally and ethically safe clinical assessments undertaken by Nurse Practitioners. This is foundational to the use of the diagnostic and clinical intervention work of Nurse Practitioners studied in later courses. This course utilises Integrated Professional Practice hours and diverse clinical practice experiences, including embedded clinical supervision, to grow advanced capabilities in clinical interviewing and assessment as the students begin to take up the identity of the Nurse Practitioner.
learning_outcomes: critically evaluate the evidence underpinning the Nurse Practitioner Scope and Standards of Practice, in light of primary health care, and professional, cultural, geographical, technological, political, legislative and ethical frameworks
apply advanced understanding, specialised skills and evidence-informed judgements to the safe undertaking of complex history taking and comprehensive clinical examination
demonstrate advanced knowledge of pathophysiology, particularly as it applies to an individual Nurse Practitioner metaspecialty
display advanced capability in high-level communication, consultation and referral, and with emerging technologies
critically analyse Nurse Practitioner and other health services for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples, vulnerable populations, and individuals and communities with diverse needs

title: Ageing and Health
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: In this course students will examine the determinants of health of older people, including those from culturally and linguistically diverse groups. Evidence that supports the health of older people will also be covered. Students will then apply this knowledge to assess and plan care of an older person using best practice approaches. The student will also develop a strategy that supports older people’s health.
learning_outcomes: Explain the factors that influence the health of older people
Use evidence to assess the health of an older person and plan care
Define and discuss the benefits of supporting Healthy Ageing
Develop a health promotion strategy for a target group of older people
Describe and evaluate the health of older people

title: Advanced Practice: Diagnostics and Interventions
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course further develops students' advanced capabilities in clinical assessment and diagnosis in order to plan the implementation of high quality, person-centred care independently/in collaboration with the interprofessional team. Using a strong theoretical basis, students build on their knowledge of pathophysiology to inform their advanced practice through clinical assessment, diagnostic decision-making through the formation of diagnoses/differential diagnoses, the ordering and interpreting of diagnostics tests, and the quality use of medicines. Students grow their advanced capabilities in making evidence-informed preventative, diagnostic, and therapeutic responses, including referrals.
learning_outcomes: critically analyse evidence-informed clinical diagnosis and care planning including choice and use of diagnostics
critically analyse diagnostic and interventional issues for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples, vulnerable populations, and individuals and communities with diverse needs
demonstrate the ability to make evidence-informed preventative and/or therapeutic responses, including the prescription of medications and referrals
synthesise complex theories of health assessment and diagnostic reasoning for safe clinical decision-making
apply advanced knowledge of pathophysiology to comprehensive physical, social and psychological assessments
undertake effective communication for autonomous and collaborative advanced practice in the context of the multidisciplinary team

assessment_tasks.task_name: Professional Practice Portfolio & Workbook (MNP students) - Pass/Fail

title: Nurse Practitioner Identity
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This is the capstone course for the Master of Nurse Practitioner program where students prepare to fully take up their Nurse Practitioner identity. Critically analysing their advanced clinical practice, students (re)turn their gaze to the professional responsibilities and technologies of their professional self as a Nurse Practitioner in Australia. Students will have multiple opportunities to engage with specialist theory and final skills development to enhance their growth as an advanced clinician. With their proven theoretical and clinical readiness, shown particularly through the achievement of the NMBA Nurse Practitioner Standards for Practice, students will be able to seek endorsement, on program completion, as a Nurse Practitioner with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. This course utilises Integrated Professional Practice hours, including embedded clinical supervision, to assist students meet the final learning outcomes in the Master of Nurse Practitioner program.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate meeting the NMBA Nurse Practitioner Standards for Practice to show theoretical and clinical readiness to seek endorsement as a Nurse Practitioner with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia

Critically analyse major processes in healthcare, for example, informatics, cultural safety, education, research, leadership, technology and/or business through the needs of clients/patients/groups/communities

Clearly articulate the complexities of the Nurse Practitioner identity in the present, and projected into the foreseeable future, considering the domains of clinical, education, leadership and research for the Nurse Practitioner
Demonstrate advanced understanding of risk and measurement for continuous improvement in Nurse Practitioner practice, particularly as they apply to the Nurse Practitioner metaspecialties

Critically analyse, and undertake, advanced clinical assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation and evaluation of care for individuals/groups/communities, including the choice and use of diagnostics, both pathology and medical imaging, and the prescription of medicines

title: Cultural Context of Custody
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Custodial Health is a complex area of healthcare delivered in a variety of custodial and corrective environments. You will have the opportunity to develop your knowledge and enhance your skills to enable you to work effectively with individuals in contact with the criminal justice system. By exploring the impact that social determinants of health have on an individual's custodial journey, in your capacity as a health professional to maintain, promote and improve the health and well-being of individuals in custody will be developed. Further to this, you will explore the national and international standards of practice and legislative frameworks in which your practice occurs. System, clinical, cultural, and interpersonal issues, specific to custodial health, will be examined, providing you with the opportunity to develop skills in facilitating person-centred, culturally safe care.
learning_outcomes: Develop an understanding of the range of diversity within custodial populations and evaluate issues related to cultural safety and vulnerable populations (such as Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people) relevant to the delivery of care in custodial environments
Demonstrate knowledge of the complexities of delivering quality healthcare in custodial environments
Demonstrate familiarity with current legislative requirements of custody in the context which they practice
Discuss the value of interdisciplinary communication and how individual practitioners participate in this process

Reflect on one's own personal values and attitudes arising when working with people whose behaviour and presentation is challenging and confronting. Identify and resolve ethical dilemmas which specifically arise when working in the custodial environments

Recognise the social determinants of health and the possibility of a history of psychological trauma experienced by people in contact with the criminal justice systems and how this influences incarceration rates

title: Advanced Symptom Management in Clinical Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course examines the role of advanced practice nurses in supporting people and their families in the assessment and management of symptoms. Students will gain knowledge of clinical reasoning and comprehensive assessment. Students will translate evidence-based practice related to symptoms and management.
learning_outcomes: Justify advanced practice nursing knowledge in symptom management
Appreciate the experience and impact of symptoms on patients, families and communities
Integrate clinical reasoning to holistic symptom management and evaluation
Demonstrate application of evidence-based comprehensive assessment

title: Perinatal Mental Health for Health Professionals
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The Perinatal Mental Health for Health Professionals course examines the psychological health and wellbeing of women and birthing people, their infants and families during pregnancy and in the first year after their baby’s birth - the perinatal period. The course challenges healthcare professionals to critically analyse concepts, content, emerging evidence, safety and barriers concerning mental health screening and assessment in the perinatal period, information sharing, cultural considerations, risk factors, indicators, referral pathways, treatments, and initial and ongoing care for women and birthing people with perinatal mental health issues (and their support people). The intent is to augment fundamental prior knowledge for healthcare professionals with more developed specialist knowledge, skills and critical thinking to assist in the provision of person-centred, evidence-based care to women and birthing people, and their babies, and where appropriate to professionally assist parenting partners, other children, family and their support people as well as contribute to workplace evidence-based enhancements in identifying, managing and supporting women and birthing people with perinatal mental health issues.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate complex understandings of the mental health issues experienced by women and birthing people, during pregnancy and in the first year after their babies’ birth; and be able to reflect critically on theory and professional practice in relation to perinatal mental health

Apply cognitive, technical and creative skills to investigate, analyse and synthesise complex information, concepts and theories, challenges and gaps and where possible apply established theories to different bodies of knowledge or practice in relation to perinatal mental health; awareness raising, screening, assessment, management and treatment
Critically evaluate the major approaches and barriers to the assessment, care and treatment of women with perinatal mental health issues and/or illnesses
Incorporate key concepts of health and access to health resources for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, diverse and ethnic families during the perinatal period

Identify and engage appropriate support services and/or referral pathways for pregnant women, mothers (their infant and partners) who require particular care, as well as personal and professional support for nurses and midwives
Identify and critically evaluate the effect of support systems such as the woman’s, family, social and professional supports have on the psychological health of the mother and their baby

title: Clinical Practice A
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This core course provides Master of Nurse Practitioner students with the opportunity to understand and design their scope of practice and service model including an evaluation framework. Students will research and synthesise clinical governance processes, legal, ethical, cultural drivers of health and advanced practice nursing provision, health policy and reforms. Students apply these determinants to Nurse Practitioner Scope of Practice and service models that focus on the provision of safe, efficient quality services including evaluation framework within the context of their clinical specialty and contemporary healthcare which will improvement in health outcomes for people and efficient, safe and quality nursing models for communities leading the advancement of nursing practice. This course Includes Integrated Professional Practice hours and diverse clinical practice experiences, including embedded clinical supervision facilitating advanced practice nursing.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the significance of the Nurse Practitioner Scope and Standards of Practice determinants in relation to regulatory compliance and legislative requirements of endorsement and practice within the student's clinical context.
Critique relevant contemporary holistic healthcare service models (local models), design methodologies and principles of evidenced based practices.
Explore current Clinical Governance, Risk, Compliance, evaluation and health metrics used to measure safe, effective, quality clinical performance, business proficiency and lead practice improvement.

Identify and Interpret key local determinants of health that influence policy and reforms, inclusive of those that impact Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, vulnerable populations and the diverse needs of the local community.

Interpret and integrate health informatics and technology processes within the student's clinical context, accounting for regulatory and governance (safety and risk) impacts and practice improvements.
Research and synthesise the body of evidence, core nursing theories, legal, and ethical practices underpinning Nurse Practitioner Scope and Standards of Practice.

Design and evaluate a Nurse Practitioner Scope of Practice and Service Model relevant to the student's clinical context and responsive to the workplace environment by critical analysis of the body of evidence.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Annotated Bibliography for Nurse Practitioner Practice Development Part B
Literature Search Nurse Practitioner Practice Development Part A
Nurse Practitioner Practice Scope of Practice

title: Teaching and Learning in the Clinical Context
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course is premised on the understanding that effective clinical teaching and learning can transform practice and practice environments. It explores theories relevant to adult learning, models of clinical teaching, how the clinical organisation influences teaching and learning, and contemporary approaches for improving clinical teaching. Students will be provided with opportunities to integrate their developing knowledge and skills into their own clinical practice and to reflect on and learn from this experience.
learning_outcomes: Examine the issue of teaching and learning in terms of nurses'/midwives' responsibilities for ongoing professional education of themselves and others
Describe teaching and learning associated with using clinical simulation in the clinical context
Discuss the implications of information and communication technology on clinical teaching and learning
Discuss and apply adult learning theories to the role of clinical teaching
Discuss creating a learning community in the clinical context
Discuss mentoring, preceptoring and clinical supervision and how they contribute to teaching and learning in the clinical context
Explain why feedback and evaluation are important and appropriate strategies for these components of clinical teaching
Recognise and describe the key elements of learning situations including learner characteristics, learning barriers and facilitators, and effective teaching strategies

assessment_tasks.task_name: Presentation of Clinical Teaching Plan with interview
Critical Reflection on Learning in a Clinical Context

title: Leadership and Change Management in Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course assists students to build on existing knowledge and will expand leadership and change management capabilities from within a health care context. The course provides learners with an opportunity to use reflective practice and both leadership and change theories to critique and analyse a workplace issue and redevelop a strategy to enable evidence-based, meaningful leadership and sustainable workplace change.
learning_outcomes: Design and justify a comprehensive change management plan informed by leadership theories, organisational analysis, and best practice evidence.

Investigate ethical, cultural (inclusive of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people), and organisational factors that influence leadership, collaboration, and decision-making in complex health systems
Evaluate personal and professional leadership styles using reflective practice to identify strengths, limitations, and areas for growth in self and others.
Critically analyse contemporary leadership and change management theories and their application within health care contexts

title: Palliative Care Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course is designed to facilitate nursing health professionals extend their knowledge of palliative and end of life care and examine palliative and end of life care practice. The course will examine the core concepts related to palliative care, including symptom assessment and management, evidenced based practice, psychological states, pharmacology, cultural and spiritual care elements, and ethical issues. End of life care across all care settings will be explored. Students are encouraged to consider and reflect on the issues and challenges arising when caring for palliative and end of life care patients in their current care context.
learning_outcomes: Critically discuss symptom assessment and management, including relevant pharmacology;
Identify current approaches in grief and bereavement care
Use an inquiring, creative and analytical approach to palliative care and end of life care nursing;
Continue to develop critical reflective skills and self evaluation of your own personal professional practice.
Examine ethical issues in palliative care and end of life care practice;
Demonstrate an in-depth knowledge of palliative care and end of life care nursing practice;
Describe optimal end of life care provision;
Recognise cultural and spiritual elements relating to end of life;

title: Introduction to Research in Health Care
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course will introduce students to the various approaches to conducting research in health care. Students will learn about study planning and design and will develop an awareness of important considerations in study design. Students will also learn to review and critique published research and reviews of published studies.
learning_outcomes: Develop health care research questions and select study designs and research processes that are suitable for answering them
Review and critically evaluate a published study or literature review using a recognised critical appraisal instrument
Describe the purpose of undertaking research in health care
Outline the components of quantitative, qualitative and mixed method study designs.

Identify and describe important considerations in study design including: ethical implications and vulnerable populations including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, and ensuring rigour in research.

title: Introduction to Occupational Therapy
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to fundamental concepts in Occupational Therapy (OT). Students examine theoretical models of practice applicable to OT practice. They also consider the OT process and are introduced to the development and implementation of appropriate OT interventions. Concepts and skills include the therapeutic use of meaningful occupation in various contexts of practice, analysis of occupational behaviour, the development of therapeutic activity programs and occupational performance issues relevant to humans.
learning_outcomes: Understanding and skills in applying theoretical models relevant to Occupational Therapy practice.
An understanding of the Occupational Therapy process.
An understanding of the philosophy and scope of Occupational Therapy.
Elementary skills in the analysis and application of the use of activity as a therapeutic tool.
Understanding of typical developmental and lifespan issues relevant to Occupational Therapy.

title: Group Processes in Occupational Therapy
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course will provide students with foundational knowledge and skills necessary to be able to participate as an effective group member and plan and lead group activities in appropriate contexts of practice in both physical and mental health settings. Content will include principles of group dynamics, models of group development, principles of group leadership, processes involved in planning and implementing groups. Workshops will provide students with the opportunity for experiential learning.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and describe their own contribution as a member of a group.
Identify and discuss elements of group dynamics.
Analyse the roles and contribution of others in a group
Apply knowledge of group work in planning and leading a group session.

title: Introduction to Occupational Therapy Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course builds upon the fundamental concepts introduced in OCCT1110, through classroom learning of practice skills and a professional placement. The students consider the application of frames of reference to the occupational therapy process. This course is Compulsory Program Component and students must pass in order to progress in the Bachelor of Occupational Therapy program.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of how occupational therapy practice is influenced by context.
Develop an understanding of what constitutes a professional, competent and ethical occupational therapist.
Demonstrate a knowledge of the underlying theory involved in occupational therapy practice skills.
Demonstrate understanding of how theoretical models are applied to occupational therapy practice.
Acquire occupational therapy practice skills appropriate to a first year level.

title: Knowledge Translation in Health Care
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course provides students' with the knowledge skills to implement evidence into healthcare policy and practice using contemporary knowledge translation methods. Knowledge translation is a dynamic and iterative process that includes synthesis, dissemination, exchange and application of knowledge to improve health and strengthen the health care system.
learning_outcomes: Design a knowledge translation project to improve knowledge use
Develop a plan to evaluate the impact of the knowledge translation project on knowledge use
Identify an area of policy and practice in need of knowledge translation
Analyse contemporary methods for knowledge translation in healthcare
Assess the barriers to knowledge use and identify potential mitigators

title: Occupational Therapy and Everyday Living
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course develops the student's knowledge of everyday living skills involved in daily occupations in context of professional practice. It develops their knowledge, skills and attitudes related to the person-environment-occupation [PEO]. The student will apply this knowledge in analysing the potential effects of disruption to body structure or function according to the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (ICF) (World Health Organisation, 2001). They will understand how occupational therapy can maximise the potential for individuals to participate in their chosen occupations. They will apply their knowledge of biomechanical principles to promote participation in everyday living skills. The student will study the practical skills utilising the evidence base that is involved in the assessment and interventions used to implement a therapeutic program for people with occupational issues involving their everyday living skills. Case based learning [CBL] will be an integral method for achieving learning outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Be competent in collaborating to establish person-centred goals.
Distinguish how the individual impact of the medical condition affects a person in their daily occupation.
Synthesise this knowledge to the application of the occupational therapy process.
Comprehend the relationship between conditions and the Occupational Therapy process in the context of professional practice.
Demonstrate relevant assessment skills needed for professional practice.
Demonstrate their knowledge and understanding of how functional anatomy and medical conditions affect occupational issues and the relevant evidence base practice (EBP) to accompany this knowledge
Begin developing person-centred intervention strategies which consider all occupational issues in relation to everyday living.

title: Enabling Occupation: Mental Health and Wellbeing
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course aims to develop the student's learning about the person-environment-occupation [PEO] interface and its impact on occupational performance with a focus on mental health and wellbeing. Through participation in this course students will develop knowledge, skills and attitudes essential for practice with people who have, or are at risk of having, disorders of mental health including: understanding of how mental disorders impact on an individual's occupational performance and participation, application of relevant theoretical frameworks, implementation of the occupational therapy process including assessment, intervention and evaluation, evidence based practice and the context of practice including policy, legal and ethical issues.
learning_outcomes: Plan appropriate occupational therapy interventions to enhance the occupational performance and participation of people with mental health problems and mental illness.
Describe the impact of mental health problems and mental illness on occupational performance and participation..
Apply theoretical frameworks when reasoning about occupational therapy intervention for people with mental health problems and mental illness.

Demonstrate consideration of the context of practice including policy, legal and ethical issues when planning occupational therapy interventions for people with mental health problems or mental illness.

title: Motor and Process Abilities in Occupations
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course introduces the student to possible occupational issues associated with the motor and process abilities of a person. This includes the Person Environment Occupation [PEO] relationship. The student will study the effects of neurological conditions on motor and processing abilities through case (or client) based scenarios [CBL]. The course develops student knowledge and application of assessments and interventions relevant to motor and processing abilities within the occupational therapy process based on evidence based practice principles.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise and apply this knowledge to the application of the occupational therapy process for people with neurological conditions.
Analyse how neurological conditions affect a persons motor and processing abilities in their daily occupations including the effect on person- environment occupation [PEO].
Demonstrate the ability to develop client-centeredness while considering occupational issues.
Demonstrate their ability to apply and reflect on the professional reasoning and behaviours.
Link knowledge in neurological conditions to the occupational therapy process in the context of professional practice.
Demonstrate their knowledge and understanding of how neurological conditions effect occupational issues.
Demonstrate competence in assessment skills.

title: Communication for Occupational Therapy Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course will assist in developing effective communication or interpersonal skills, including the four macro skills: speaking, listening, writing and reading in the context of inter-professional teams, groups and individuals. It forms foundational knowledge, skills and attitudes for Occupational Therapy Practice.
learning_outcomes: Examine and respond to the needs associated with various factors influencing effective communication during Occupational Therapy practice, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.
Use the various components of spoken and written communicative skills to achieve effective Occupational therapy practice, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.
Explore and reflect upon the strengths and weakness of their personal communication style in both face-to-face and non face-to-face contexts.
Interpret and respond to spoken and written communication in ways that reflect effective OT practice, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.

title: Beginning Professional Practice in Occupational Therapy
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This is the second of four practice placement courses in the undergraduate occupational therapy programme. The course aims to broaden the students professional practice experience while assisting them to consolidate their academic knowledge and develop their clinical skills. Seven weeks of professional practice placement is embedded into the thirteen-week course. The students undertake their practice placements off campus in a variety of service settings.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate effective reflective practitioner skills

Demonstrate an understanding of how to assess a clients, needs, identity and prioritise performance issues, establish clear client centred goals, select and implement appropriate OT interventions and evaluate their own practice.
Demonstrate an understanding of the minimum competency standards for graduating OT's (as per OT Australia 2010)
Demonstrate emerging clinical competence by completing each of the learning objectives in the 8 domains of the SPER-R
Demonstrate how theoretical models of OT can guide assessment and intervention choices in practice

title: Environmental Contexts of Occupational Therapy Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: In Australia, a key role of occupational therapists is adapting environmental contexts. This may include modifying individual homes, schools, transport facilities, and other local amenities and buildings which people with disabling conditions need to access during their daily routines. This breadth of perspective also requires an awareness of how physical and sensory issues impact on an individual. It also requires an understanding of their social and cultural environment and the occupational concept of "place." When integrating theory and practice to adapt environmental contexts an occupational therapist requires an advanced level of technical skills and appropriate professional reasoning incorporating consideration of the needs of the person and significant others.
learning_outcomes: Assess and analyse the impact of the environment (home/community/social/political/cultural) on a person's occupational task performance.
Evaluate a client's home or community environment, determining necessary modification according to AS1428.1 and National Construction Codes, for improved occupational performance.
Select domestic and community activities appropriate to the needs and abilities of the client.
Critically appraise the modification for improving the quality of life of the person/family and relevant others.
Clearly describe practice reasoning for all proposed recommendations.
Accurately measure specific relevant dimensions of the home of relevant Persons/clients
Draw clear sketches & technical drawings of modifications and positions for rails in bathrooms and toilets, according to AS1428.1 and National Construction Codes.

title: Enabling Occupation in Productivity
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Productivity includes the paid and unpaid occupations that humans do to produce goods or services, provide sense of belonging in a community, and contribute to meeting the needs of others in society. This course addresses: 1) the meaning of productive occupations for all individuals, inclusive of health status, identity, disability, employability, employment status, and age and 2) the diverse roles occupational therapists’ hold within the practice of enabling productive occupation. Course content includes: a) evidence-informed models of practice, clinical reasoning, assessment, communication, and intervention skills needed for creating ergonomically and psychologically safe paid and unpaid productive occupation and b) how to enable productive occupations for individuals who are neurodiverse, aging, and/or experience mental health issues, occupational injustice and/or intellectual disabilities.
learning_outcomes: Explain how occupational therapists practice across the field of work rehabilitation and in enabling participation in productive occupation.
Justify the role of occupational therapy for enabling productive occupation within traditional and non-traditional/emerging practice.
Analyse the relationship between a worker, work and the environment and that of a person, their productive occupation and their environments.
Evaluate a client's capacity to work and return to work.
Communicate and collaborate effectively, in both oral and written form, independently and within a group, using the appropriate conventions of the discipline.
Formulate a viable plan to enable transition within or re-entry into work/productive occupation.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Return to Work Plan Case Conference

title: Intermediate Professional Practice in Occupational Therapy
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This is the third of four practice placement courses in the undergraduate occupational therapy program. The course aims to broaden the students professional practice experience while assisting them to consolidate their academic knowledge and develop their clinical skills. Eight weeks of professional practice placement is embedded into this thirteen-week course. The students undertake their practice placements off campus in a variety of service setting.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an ability to evaluate their own practice along with the policy and practices of those in the service setting in which they have undertaken their placement, in light of current best practice and research evidence. Then suggest how they might improve future practice in this service setting as appropriate.
Demonstrate an understanding of the Minimum Competency Standards for graduating OT's (The Australian Occupational Therapy Standards)

Demonstrate a good understanding of how to assess a client's needs, identify and prioritize performance issues, establish clear client centred goals, select and implement appropriate OT interventions and evaluate intervention outcomes.
Demonstrate sound clinical /ethical reasoning skills by defending the decisions they have made in relation their chosen case study and clinical incident.
Demonstrate how theoretical models of OT can be used to guide their assessment selection and intervention choices in practice
Demonstrate intermediate clinical competence by completing each of the learning objectives in all of the eight domains of the revised version of the Student Practice Evaluation Form (SPEF-R)

title: Occupational Justice in Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Occupations, i.e., the meaningful things people do, are innately human and a determinant of health. In this course, students deeply explore the concepts and research associated with occupation, occupational science, occupational justice and occupational injustice as they relate to occupational therapy practice. Students critically analyse the structural and contextual influences on occupation, for populations of people in our "local" communities. This course emphasizes population-based practice, advocacy as intervention, persuasive communication, innovation and leadership as essential to service delivery for today's occupational therapists. Students engage in analytical, practical and reflective learning, to promote occupational justice in practice and our community.
learning_outcomes: Communicate and collaborate effectively, in both oral and written form, independently and within pairs, using the appropriate conventions of the discipline.
Envision making our community more occupationally just
Differentiate between occupation, occupational science, occupational therapy, occupational justice and occupational injustice;
Appreciate the complex nature of occupation;
Analyse how societal, structural and contextual factors and stakeholders influence occupation, identity, health and participation for our clients, i.e., populations or individuals.
Apply occupational justice, population-based practice, advocacy as intervention, persuasive communication, innovation and leadership to occupational therapy practice.

title: Occupational Science in National and International Contexts
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course examines the relationship of occupation, health and wellbeing, from a national and international perspective. Students will have the opportunity to evaluate the adequacy of the predominantly "Western" approach found in much occupational science literature when considering the relationship between these three concepts. They will evaluate the adequacy of this approach when describing the links between occupation, health, and well-being for culturally diverse communities both in Australia and throughout the world.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the application of occupational science to occupational therapy in Australia and throughout the world
Examine your perception of health and occupation as a point of reference in working with others
Demonstrate preparedness for contextually-relevant, occupation-centred practice with diverse persons and populations

Analyse the cultural, political, economic, technological, social and environmental factors that influence the relationship between occupation, health and wellbeing for individuals, communities and populations nationally and internationally

title: Researching  an Occupational Therapy Intervention
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course requires students to review a selected area of Occupational Therapy (OT) practice in order to identify gaps in service provision or unfulfilled client needs that require development of an OT intervention. In some cases the intervention will be linked directly to the needs of the professional community. This intervention development requires the student to perform an international literature review that researches and critically evaluates the available literature relating to the identified need and possible current uses of the proposed intervention. It also requires the students to apply relevant OT theory linking the theoretical assumptions and evidence with the proposed intervention.
learning_outcomes: Present a well organised outline of the proposed intervention, including it's rationale, purpose, aim and objectives.
Select the most appropriate occupation focused model, and where relevant, a frame of reference to guide the design and content of the intervention.
Identify a gap and/or need within current occupational therapy practice.
Indicate methods of evaluating the intervention objectives using both standardised and non-standardised instruments.
Design a proposed intervention relevant to the identified gap or need.
Analyse and synthesise relevant literature to provide a clear rationale for the proposed intervention design, content and delivery.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Essay / Written Assignments No 1 - Providing Evidence
Essay / Written Assignments No 2 - Describing the intervention

title: Promoting Health and Wellbeing in Occupational Therapy Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to develop knowledge and skills relevant to the role of occupational therapy in health promotion and prevention of illness and disability. Students will learn about determinants of health and health inequalities, principles of health promotion and how these are addressed in occupational therapy practice with a particular emphasis on lifestyle, balance and the role of leisure. Learning will take place through a combination of lectures, workshop sessions and independent activities, underpinned by the principles of experience-based learning.
learning_outcomes: Develop and evaluate occupational therapy interventions for health promotion and leisure participation for individual, group and population level practice
Outline the association between leisure and health and wellbeing and the role of leisure in health promotion and prevention
Determine the existence of and factors contributing to health inequalities for a given population group.
Apply appropriate theoretical frameworks, research evidence and policy to inform clinical reasoning around interventions targeting health promotion and leisure participation
Outline the principles of health promotion and prevention in occupational therapy practice.

title: Children, Youth and Families: An Occupational Approach
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: The course explores the development and occupational functioning of children, youth within families. It will examine various aspects of childhood/youth and related conditions along with associated occupational needs. Students will develop understanding of relevant assessments, important aspects of functioning during childhood/youth and interventions used for children/youth.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the relevance of play in development
Demonstrate understanding of developmental milestones
Develop relevant Family/Person-centred goals and interventions.
Demonstrate understanding of relevant standardised assessments for particular children/youth
Appraise skills and barriers to child occupational performance as they relate to specific disabilities and disorders
Determine how to enable occupational engagement of children and youth in their chosen play/leisure, self-care and productivity occupations.
Create a plan for assessment and treatment based on knowledge of skills and barriers to child occupational performance
Express knowledge of common childhood disorders and associated occupational needs.

title: Advanced Professional Practice in Occupational Therapy
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This is the fourth and final placement courses in the undergraduate occupational therapy program. The course aims to broaden student professional practice experience while assisting them to consolidate their academic knowledge and clinical skills. A block professional practice experience is embedded in this course. Students undertake their placements off campus in a variety of service settings. This is a compulsory programme component and students must pass in order to progress in the Bachelor of Occupational Therapy Programme.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate graduate level clinical reasoning skills through the concise and logical presentation of the decisions made in relation to a chosen practice incident and the robust defence of these during an exit interview.

Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of how to assess client needs; identify and prioritize their occupational performance issues; establish clear client-centred goals; select and implement appropriate OT interventions and evaluate and refine their own practice by completing a job application.

Demonstrate how they have met the Minimum Competency Standards for Graduating OTs, as published by OT Australia (2010), by providing verbal examples and written evidence from their e-portfolio during an exit interview exam.

Demonstrate graduate level clinical competence by independently completing each of the learning objectives in all eight domains of the revised version of the Student Practice Evaluation Form (SPEF-R) sufficient to satisfactorily pass their final practice placement.

title: Transitioning into Occupational Therapy Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course aims to form a bridge between professional learning in the undergraduate program and the student's entry into professional practice. This will be achieved through the use of case studies, with expectations for clinical reasoning and appraisal of available literature and evidence. Students will synthesize theoretical and practical learning gained throughout the occupational therapy program, apply this knowledge to new cases, and utilize critical analysis and clinical reasoning to plan assessment and intervention. Students will examine such factors as, contexts of practice, theoretical approaches, ethical and moral issues, political and legal contexts, and social and cultural influence, in developing written work. Additionally students will also appraise their current strengths and ongoing professional development priorities. Advanced workshops designed to refine professional skills will be presented.
learning_outcomes: Be proactive in their professional development through engagement and participation in available workshops and case analyses in these final weeks;
Appraise personal practice skills to identify individual strengths and needs for continuing professional development (CPD);

Formulate case analyses, defining core aspects of identified disability, analysing functional implications, designing plans for assessment, and appraising available literature and evidence for intervention;

Analyse and synthesise the impact of factors such as contexts of practice, theoretical approaches, ethical and moral issues, political and legal contexts, and social and cultural influences on their practice;

title: OHS Practice
faculty: College of Health Medicine and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: This course considers the fundamental principles & practices of occupational safety and health management systems in a wide range of working environments with reference to Singapore OHS legislation. The course is only offered externally in Singapore and focuses on experiential learning and problem based learning (pbl) techniques.
